1	# Item & Module Database
2	
3	> Authoring guidance: .claude/docs/templates/guidance/game-design-document-guide.md (load per-section as you author — do not read entirely).
4	
5	> **Status**: Designed
6	> **Author**: user + game-designer, economy-designer, systems-designer, creative-director (via /design-system, autonomous; orchestrated run 2026-10-26)
7	> **Last Updated**: 2026-10-28 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix and delegated rulings)*
8	> **Last Verified**: 2026-10-27 (against the Graph's 2026-10-27 amendment)
9	> **Index position**: Systems Enumeration row **3** (`systems-index.md`, "Item & Module Database (inferred)", Economy, MVP) and Recommended Design Order **6** (Feature layer). The Overview rationale bullet is "**3. Item & Module Database**". Both numberings mean this system.
10	> **Implements Pillar**: P5 Deeper Is Richer, Loss Is Not Total (primary — the catalogue is the vocabulary of the only faucet, salvage; a patch is capped at `PATCH_CAP_BP` and only a finite salvaged part restores full, so scarcity pushes inward); P1 The World Never Lies (primary — a def holds only true values: mass, ports, ratings, repair part; a module's condition is its own output and wear in the room, never a stat a def or a card invents). **Serves**: P4 Sanity Rewrites Reality (sub-class d, phantom salvage — a true `mass_g` on every def is the falsifier the carried-weight field check reads; the lie itself is Perception's and Sanity's); P3 The Web Watches (the glowstick is a pool that counts as exposure like any other; the Item DB adds no stimulus); P2 Dread Before Chaos (indirect — parts and modules are what surviving a tell costs; no Item DB mechanic fires without one)
11	> **Creative Director Review (CD-GDD-ALIGN)**: CONCERNS → REVISED 2026-10-26 (5 items applied)
12	> **Design Review (first formal review)**: 2026-10-27 — 4 BLOCKING findings (Graph reconciliation, F-12 rated flow, shed and downed rows, canonical positional encoding) and the RECOMMENDED set applied or routed; two items awaited a user decision (Open Questions 29 and 32), **both now resolved by user rulings (X6/D19 and D18)**. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the pending-decision wording is withdrawn)*
13	> **Design Re-review**: 2026-10-27 — 3 BLOCKING findings (patch-history and `hp`-0 yields that the validator would refuse; the Interaction holder losing the patch cap) and the RECOMMENDED set applied or routed; the open items are Open Questions 46 to 55. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
14	> **Cross-GDD and delegated-ruling pass**: 2026-10-28 — the IDB-16 holders are conformed (Interaction IA-28/IA-36, Suit SE-12/SE-13/SE-38, Save/Load SL-2; Open Question 47 resolved by G6), the pure constructor `fresh_instance` is added (IDB-28), F-11 gains the demand-1 band exemption and its example reads the tightened 4-part ledger (800; Open Questions 38 and 55 resolved by G2), the reference machines RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK are named (R12), and Open Questions 1 to 5 are decided by R20/R21. This pass: `mod_scrubber` joins the node-lantern defs (`emits` LANTERN, `base_pm` 200 [PH], `LANTERN_O2`; five `emits` defs; IDB-31, AC-26, AC-97), per ruling G6, to match the registry's 8 lanterns. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
15	
16	## Summary
17	
18	The Item & Module Database is the game's read-only catalogue of the 23 physical things that can be cut free, carried, installed, held, spent or thrown: thirteen ship modules, three hand tools, a glowstick, five repair parts and a data core, each with a true mass, the pipes and wires it fits, and the one part that fully mends it. It exists because salvage is the game's only source of anything: nothing is bought or crafted, a salvaged module keeps the damage and the patch cap it died with, and a patch can only hold a module at 60 percent until a finite part cut from another wreck makes the repair last. Read it if you design anything that places, carries, installs, repairs or saves an item, or if you need a stable id or a weight for one. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: the count falls from 24 to 23 and the hand tools from four to three because `tool_suppressant` leaves the MVP roster (X6, D19; it stays a dormant reserved id, IDB-4); the stowed hull plate disables `run` (D18, IDB-13).)*
19	
20	> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Feature` · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `Life-Support Graph (designed; hard: node kinds, port-type ids, M5/M6/M7)`, `Command & Simulation Layer (designed; soft: BOOTING order, no block)`, `Player Controller & Input (designed; soft: PC-8, V_CARRY)`, `Pixel-Perfect Pipeline and art bible (designed; soft: TILE_PX, sprite cells)`; downstream, all designed as of 2026-10-27 (each repeats its own clause in its own GDD): Suit & Equipment, Ship Section & Layout, Modular Ship Assembly, Derelict Authoring, Boarding & Salvage, Interaction, Emitter State, Save/Load *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: stale "undesigned/in flight" labels removed)*
21	
22	## Overview
23	
24	The Item & Module Database is the game's **static, read-only catalogue of every physical thing that can be cut free, carried, installed, held, spent or thrown** — twenty-three definitions ("defs") in the MVP *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: was twenty-four; `tool_suppressant` is removed from the MVP roster by the user ruling of X6 / D19, and stays a dormant reserved id, IDB-4)* across six classes (module, tool, consumable, repair part, curio, and a reserved junk class) — and each def fixes only what its thing *is* (a true mass, the ports it exposes, its ratings, the part that mends it) and what it *fits* (a Graph node kind and port types, a carry class). Nothing on a def says what the thing is *worth*: there is no price, rarity, recipe or loot weight anywhere in the catalogue, because salvage is the only faucet in the game and a thing's value is whatever the ship will not do without it. The catalogue is loaded once in BOOTING as an immutable `ItemCatalog`; it registers **no kernel state block, no step hook, no command and no mutator** (the kernel's Interactions table has no Item DB row), so it can be called from `validate`, from P3 and from presentation as a set of pure queries. Two keys identify a def: the string `def_id` — the **only** item key that ever reaches a save, a snapshot, a `SalvageRecord` or a hash — and an append-only numeric `type_id` that exists for in-memory tables and later replication summaries and never reaches persisted data, so renumbering can never break a save. The Graph owns the loop ids, node kinds and port-type ids; the Item DB consumes them by number and never defines one. The Item DB also defines the single `ItemInstance` value schema that every holder (the Suit's per-player block, a loose-world placement, a Graph node about to be salvaged) embeds in its own block, because Suit, Assembly, Boarding and Save/Load must serialise the same shape; it stores, allocates and moves no instance itself.
25	
26	The player never meets "the database"; they meet its consequences as things with a body. A Foundry scrubber cut from derelict A's dead bus arrives at the home-ship carrying the condition it died with — still dark, still FAILED — because a def never refreshes what the Graph recorded. It is hauled at the locked flat carry speed with both hands full and the chest lamp still lit, installed into a hardpoint it physically fits, and patched, which the Graph caps at `PATCH_CAP_BP` 6000; only a **repair part**, itself cut from another wreck and spent once, restores the full ceiling and ends the patch's decay clock; cutting a patched module out and putting it back lifts nothing. A glowstick is one finite pool of Chemlight (`#86B896`) that counts as exposure like any other light. A carried module's mass is reported to the player by their own body (breath, strain — the Suit's consequence-channel cue), never by a number, a bar or a pack screen. And because every def carries a true mass and never a believed one, a phantom crate that looks like a data core can be caught by how it weighs (hallucination sub-class d, vertical slice) — the catalogue is the thing being lied about, never the liar. The two anchor numbers the rest of the game reads from it are small and exact: an item's `def_id` (what it is) and its `mass_g` (how much of it there is).
27	
28	Without this system, salvage and welding have nothing to act on, and each neighbour (Assembly, Interaction, Suit, Derelict Authoring, Boarding, Layout) would invent its own item vocabulary until the save format broke on every module change — the concept's named technical risk ("save format not versioned from v1"). With it, the home-ship stays "a body assembled from the corpses of other ships" (concept, Core Fantasy) in the strictest sense: every object in it has a provenance, a dialect, a condition and a true weight, and none was bought, crafted or minted. The index flags this system as a **quiet bottleneck** — nine dependents (five in the MVP: Suit & Equipment, Ship Section & Layout Data Model, Modular Ship Assembly, Derelict Authoring, Boarding & Salvage) — so the schema is frozen early, versioned from v1 (`catalogue_version`), and kept data-contract shaped even though `modes.workflow: full` requires the whole template.
29	
30	**Index wording, reconciled.** The index rationale reads: "Definitions of salvageable modules (scrubber, reactor cell, hull plate, coolant unit, data core), tools, consumables and their dialect and weights; references graph port-type IDs that the Life-Support Graph GDD defines." Four of the five named modules do not map one-to-one onto a Graph node kind, and this GDD resolves them (IDB-10): the **scrubber** is `mod_scrubber` (node kind 20); the **reactor cell** is `mod_reactor_cell` (kind 10) and is *not* the battery cell, which is its own def `mod_battery_cell` (kind 11); the **coolant unit** is a roster family name over three defs (`mod_coolant_pump`, `mod_radiator`, `mod_coolant_reservoir`) because one def is exactly one Graph node; the **hull plate** is a *repair part* (`part_hull_plate`), not a module, because a HULL_SEGMENT has no `def_id` and `salvage_node` refuses it — a conflict with the index wording that is routed to the Graph owner (Open Questions); the **data core** is a *curio* with no Graph presence (`curio_data_core`, node kind 0), because the Graph has no data-core node kind and the concept forbids an authored story. "Dialect" is a sprite-and-port-shape field with no gameplay stat in the MVP; "weights" are true integer grams that change neither speed nor noise.
31	
32	*Citation key.* `[LSG:n]` is a line of `design/gdd/life-support-graph.md`, `[KRN:n]` of `command-simulation-layer.md`, `[PCI:n]` of `player-controller-input.md`, `[PPR:n]` of `pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md`, `[IDX:n]` of `systems-index.md`, `[CON:n]` of `game-concept.md`, `[REG:n]` of `design/registry/entities.yaml`, `[ART:n]` of `design/art/art-bible.md`, all as read on 2026-10-26; rule ids (LS-n, CR-n, PC-n) are given where one exists. Tags: **[PH]** Item DB placeholder, not a Graph or registry fact, a registry candidate; **[DECL]** declared here, validated by the Graph at data load; **[INF]** inferred from the connectability rules, routed for a one-word confirmation; **(provisional — X undesigned/in flight)** a cross-system clause the named dependent must repeat when it is written. Implementation questions raised while designing are deferred to ADR candidates, marked "-> ADR candidate": the runtime object type of a def (constrained by IDB-26: a typed `RefCounted` `ItemDef`, never a `Resource`, never static state — the ADR records the choice but may not loosen the constraints), the export include-filter for `assets/data/items/*.json`, and the catalogue-hash function. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The engine reference has **no module for this domain** (`docs/engine-reference/godot/modules/` holds animation, audio, input, navigation, networking, physics, rendering and ui; there is no `scripting.md`, `core.md`, JSON, `Resource` or export file), so every engine claim here about data loading is MEDIUM confidence and spike-bound.
33	
34	## Player Fantasy
35	
36	**Framing: an Economy system has two fantasies, and this one leads with the direct one.** *(creative-director consulted; three framings weighed — "Organs From the Dead" leads, "The Weight Is the Truth" is the hallucination beat, "Every Part Reads Like Its Pipe" is the presentation beat.)* The direct fantasy is the one the player feels while handling a thing: **salvage-surgeon**. The indirect fantasy is what the catalogue makes possible inside other systems' moments: the home-ship becomes legible history.
37	
38	> **Everything we own, we cut out of a dead ship and carried home — and it still remembers what happened to it.**
39	>
40	> The concept's Core Fantasy says the home-ship is "a body they assembled from the corpses of other ships" [CON:46-48]. The Item DB is the anatomy of that sentence: a scrubber is not loot, it is a lung taken from a corpse, and it arrives with the corpse's injuries. Nothing in this world is minted, bought or crafted; every object has a provenance (the wreck it came from, its dialect) and a condition (the `hp` the Graph recorded, carried across the cut). The player's power is not owning things. It is **knowing what a thing really is** — what it fits, what it weighs, what state it is truly in — when the world, the scanner and their own eyes are under pressure to lie.
41	
42	*Tone guard on the metaphor.* The body-and-organ language belongs to the design text and the player's own head only. It must never become visual or textual flesh: flesh tones and violet "appear nowhere in the sane world" [CON:333-334], no bare skin is ever shown [ART:508], and materials are cold metals only [ART:635-636]. Display names stay technician-plain (guard rail AP-6 below).
43	
44	**MVP anchor moment — "the splice from the cold room"** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the review found that the headline scrubber and machine-kit loop below cannot be played in the MVP, because the `scr_a` carry has no destination and no `part_machine_kit` is placed (DA-25); the MVP experience target is re-anchored on a beat the MVP slice can play).* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the "no destination" premise is superseded by user ruling D72 / DA-47, which gives `scr_a` a home slot, two vacant scrubber slots at home; the carry is now a decision with a payoff. The heater beat stays the MVP reference carry (Boarding C-BS-3); what remains Vertical Slice is only the `part_machine_kit` placement.)* It uses only MVP-placed fixtures and roster ids (Boarding BS-17, Derelict Authoring DA-25). (1) *Want and carry.* On the first sortie the reference payoff is the heater `htr_a` (`mod_heater`, 12000 g, MEDIUM) cut from derelict A and carried home at `V_CARRY`, hands full, chest lamp lit. (2) *The price shows.* Installed in the vacant home-ship socket it arms the bus overload (BS-17; DA-12): the trunk CABLE runs hot and begins to wear. (3) *Patch, hope on a clock.* A patch holds the cable at `PATCH_CAP_BP` and starts the decay clock; the player is now on the treadmill (G-0). (4) *The part, earned* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: "earned" holds for the placed splice; a lamp scrapped on purpose also yields a `part_cable_splice` until Open Question 39 is decided, F-11 `supply_max`)*. In derelict A's `a_machine`, inside the lethal cold room, lies one `part_cable_splice` (DA-25): a 5.6-second crossing and out again. A full repair spends it and the cable's ceiling returns to `HP_FULL`. The alternative fix for the broken junction is the spare `mod_breaker_junction` on A (`a_life`): a module swap; the spare is placed at full condition (`condition_bp` 10000, registry `mvp_part_ledger`), so the swap itself spends no splice *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier clause said the spare's own full repair also takes a cable splice, which a spare at full `hp` never needs)*. The arc is want, exposure, patch under a deadline, then a small part that costs a risk to fetch. **Scarcity pushed inward**, with only MVP-placed content. ET-3 is measured on this beat; ET-2 is measured on this beat and, since DA-47 / user ruling D72 gave `scr_a` a home slot, on the install of derelict A's FAILED `scr_a` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
45	
46	**Vertical Slice anchor moment — "the scrubber from derelict A".** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: relabelled; the beat needs a `part_machine_kit` placement and a destination for the `scr_a` carry, both Vertical Slice content.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the destination now exists, DA-47 / user ruling D72 supplies the home scrubber slot; only the `part_machine_kit` placement is still Vertical Slice content.)* It uses only locked fixtures and roster ids; placeholder numbers are tagged.
47	
48	1. **Want.** In derelict A the beam finds a Foundry scrubber, FAILED, authored at `hp` 2000 [LSG:228]. It sits dark — no rotor turning, no medium moving. The home-ship's own scrubber is wearing.
49	2. **Cost before the cut.** Cutting it free (V8; the cutter lists the verb, Interaction owns the command) leaves its fluid ports `open_end` until they are capped [LSG:772]. The player hears the hiss they caused.
50	3. **Carry.** `mod_scrubber` is the one carried module (illustrative; in the MVP slice the `scr_a` carry has its destination, the vacant home scrubber slot of DA-47 / user ruling D72, and the reference carry used for the numbers below stays the heater `htr_a`, Boarding & Salvage C-BS-3) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (`carry_ref` [PCI:131]): gait forced to `V_CARRY` 1 px/tick, **no run**, every `interact` mode except `drop` rejected `BUSY`; the chest lamp still lights the way [ART:512]. A 30-tile corridor (1,440 base px at `TILE_PX` 48) takes 1,440 ticks = 24 s carrying against 720 ticks = 12 s walking at `V_WALK` 2, and emits 1,440 `NOISE_PER_TICK` units against 720 (carry 1 per tick, walk 1 per tick, over twice the ticks [REG:5442-5457]). The module's mass (`mass_g` 40000, [PH]) is felt only as the Suit's body cue, never a number. This is the stretch where tells are heard (P2) and Attention is earned (P3).
51	4. **Install, then disappointment.** At home it is installed with the `hp` of the record, 2000 [LSG:184, 185]: still FAILED, still dark. The catalogue did not refresh it. The world never lies.
52	5. **Patch, hope on a clock.** A patch lifts `hp` toward, never past, `PATCH_CAP_BP` 6000. At 6000 the Graph's `eff` (cited by name, D.4) is 750 permille and the scrubber runs DEGRADED at an output of 300 mGU/step — the figure the Graph's own tuning note describes as "equals one crew — any degradation loses the room" [LSG:927]. It runs, but with zero margin and a decay clock (`PATCH_DECAY_S` 240) ticking behind it. A bolted patch plate on its casing says "we did this in a hurry" [ART:617].
53	6. **The part, earned (Vertical Slice: no `part_machine_kit` is placed in the MVP, DA-25).** Only a `part_machine_kit` — a finite thing cut from another wreck — lets a full repair restore the ceiling to `HP_FULL` and end the decay clock [LSG:222]. The part, not the timer, is what makes the next sortie necessary. **Scarcity pushed inward.**
54	
55	The emotional arc is want, exposure (the cut's hiss), dread (slow to flee, hands full) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: was "slow, loud"; F-13 shows a carried module is quieter per tile than a run and a stowed plate quieter than an empty run, so the cost is the lost escape, not volume)*, relief (home), disappointment (still dead), hope with a deadline (patch), earned competence (the part). It is the Project Zomboid "the base becomes self-sufficient" feeling [CON:52-55] with "survivable never quite certain" built into the item itself.
56	
57	**Pillar alignment.** *Pillar 5 (primary), verbatim:* "The outer ring is kept unsafe by depletion and wear (scrubbers degrade, salvage runs out), so there is no safe place to farm forever." The catalogue is the vocabulary of the only faucet: a part is finite, a patch is capped, and the faucet is bounded by the authored node count. The other half of the pillar, "Deeper Is *Richer*", is delivered by placement and never by stat: no def carries a worth, dialect is a skin and `grade` has no behaviour, so richness deeper in the web is expressed by Derelict Authoring and Depth Rings & Scarcity through placement density, part supply (`part_cover_pm` by ring, F-11) and authored `hp` (better-condition modules deeper), never through def stats (binding, IDB-29 rule 5). *Pillar 1 (primary), verbatim:* "Pipes leak, frost forms, air hisses; the physical world is ground truth. Only instruments and perception can be wrong." Every def holds only true values; a module's condition is its output in the room and the scuffs and patch plates on its body, not a field on a card. *Pillar 4(d), verbatim:* "A crate of treasure is garbage once it is home. At least one cheaper field check exists (carried weight, a second scanner, the palette leak); the trip home is the fallback, not the only reveal." The Item DB supplies the true mass that check reads. *Pillar 3* is served by the carry gait and the glowstick pool; *Pillar 2* only indirectly, because a part or module is what surviving a tell costs and the Item DB fires nothing.
58	
59	**MDA alignment** [CON:80-89]. The Item DB's felt contribution is *Challenge* (the repair economy: the part as the scarce input), *Fellowship* (the concept's rank-3 aesthetic, "crew roles (boarder vs. ship-keeper) ... a shared home-ship" [CON:84]: the haul is a division of labour. Each player has one `carry_ref` (IDB-2), so the hauler is slow to flee and hands-full (a carried module emits 1 noise unit per tick for twice the ticks of a walk, 48 per tile against 24 for a walk, and so less per tile than a run (64 per tile at 4 per tick), and a stowed plate is quieter than an empty run, 720 against 1920 units over 30 tiles: the plate's cost is the escape gait it removes, F-13) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier "slow, loud" claim did not match the F-13 arithmetic)* while a crewmate lights the way with glowsticks and guards the corridor; parts are spent per player (IDB-20 (7)) and move between crewmates only by being shed and picked up (States row 14), so who mends what is a crew decision *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the hand-over mechanism)*; and F-14's two-crew margin makes the second scrubber a shared crew goal), *Fantasy* ("a ship that is ours because we welded it") and *Discovery* (a module's real condition is learned by installing it and watching it, not by reading it). It must deliver *Competence* (reading what a salvaged thing is really worth from the world) and *Autonomy* ("which module", and "weigh a module's value against the noise of taking it" [CON:98]). It must never deliver Submission, which the concept deliberately omits: there is no comfortable stockpile.
60	
61	**Design test (Item DB-specific, falsifiable).** *A module whose condition and worth are numbers on a card vs. a module whose condition is its own output in the room and the scuffs and patch plates on its body, and whose only cure is a finite part cut from another wreck → the module with the body and the part.* It resolves two live decisions. Should a def carry a `quality`, `rarity` or `value` field shown on pickup? No: `grade` is a reserved integer that is 0 everywhere in the MVP and has no behaviour. Should a free, infinitely repeatable action restore a module to full? No: a patch caps at `PATCH_CAP_BP`, a full repair takes a part, and cutting a patched module out and putting it back does not lift the cap or stop the decay clock either (IDB-18). *Secondary test (mirrors Pillar 4's):* **a weight that slows you vs. a weight your body reports truthfully → the truthful report.** Speed and noise never scale with mass.
62	
63	**Experience targets** (playtest-checkable, not mechanics).
64	
65	| # | Target | What it proves |
66	|---|---|---|
67	| ET-1 | After the first salvage, **at least 6 of 8 testers** say where the home scrubber came from without prompting (forced free-text question after the first sortie, scored against a written key) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | provenance is felt |
68	| ET-2 | **At least 6 of 8 testers** who install a FAILED module (derelict A's FAILED `scr_a` at `hp` 2000 into a home scrubber slot, an MVP beat since DA-47 / user ruling D72, or the broken junction) reach for a patch within 30 s and none opens a menu *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: "a Vertical Slice scrubber" is stale)* | the catalogue never heals |
69	| ET-3 | **At least 6 of 8 testers** explain in their own words why a patched module still needs a part (scored against a written key: names the cap, the decay or the finite part) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | the cap reads as physical, not arbitrary |
70	| ET-4 | **At most 1 of 8 testers** asks "where is the shop" or "where is the crafting bench" within thirty minutes *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | the faucet reads as salvage-only |
71	| ET-5 (vertical slice, sub-class d) | **At least 6 of 8 testers** who carried a phantom crate home say "it felt too light" or "I should have checked" *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | the weight is the unkind truth |
72	
73	**Under hallucination the fantasy deepens rather than breaks.** The catalogue is the thing being lied about, never the liar. "We know what our things really are" becomes harder and more valuable as sanity falls; it does not collapse, because at least one channel of truth always remains [CON:261-265]. The split is the Graph's: the **consequence channel** is a closed list (compartment temperature, O2 and pressure as the body feels them; frost, mist, scorch and drip trails; the acoustic classes at a descriptor anchor; Suit body cues — breath, visor fog, rime, shiver and the rest of Suit's SE-27 set (no vignette, SE-27); lamp brightness from `served_pm`; draught) and is never corruptible; the **module-body channel** (sprites, gauges, inspect cards, a module's own wear state) may lie [LSG:44, LSG:864].
74	
75	| Hallucination class | In the MVP? | What the player sees (corruptible module-body channel) | What stays true | Effect on this fantasy |
76	|---|---|---|---|---|
77	| **(b) false system state** | **Yes** | The salvaged scrubber's sprite shows its rotor turning and no patch plate; its inspect card reads OK | The room still thins — breath, visor fog, draught, lamp brightness from `served_pm`; the def's `hp` and the Graph's output are what run | "My eyes say fixed; my breath says otherwise." The part you think you no longer need is the part you need. Deepens the lead framing |
78	| **(d) phantom salvage** | Vertical slice (VS-A) | A crate or module reads as a lure (a reactor-cell sprite) | Its true `mass_g` lies outside the lure's by at least `WEIGHT_TELL_MIN_PM` 300 [PH]; the carry body cue reports the true mass | "It breathed like a data core." The weight is the unkind truth |
79	| (a) phantom entity | not this system | — | carry noise is real and the Controller's | Carrying makes you slow and loud while things that may not be there move |
80	| (c) crewmate as horror | not this system | A crewmate carrying a module may render as a horror | the human channel (voice, their beam's colour and shape) is never faked [CON:217-219] | The crewmate hauling your scrubber home is still your crewmate |
81	
82	Three rules follow, restating decisions rather than adding any. No def field is a believed, displayed or perceived value (`appears_as`, `displayed_as`, `fake_mass`, `lure_sprite` and any `hallucination_*` key are forbidden); a `junk` def holds only its own true data. There is no "unidentified item" mechanic: a def's identity is never hidden behind an identify step, and the player who learned what `part_pipe_fitting` looks like keeps that knowledge across a reload or a death, because Pillar 5's failure contract costs ship and body, never knowledge. Identification uncertainty comes only from Pillar 4 perception, which is falsifiable. **Risk carried to Suit & Equipment:** the carried-mass body cue must ride on a cue already in the closed consequence-channel list (breath, visor fog, rime, shiver and the rest of Suit's SE-27 set; no vignette, SE-27); if Suit proposes a new cue type (a shoulder-strain frame), its owner must either add it to the closed list or accept that it is module-body, corruptible, and so cannot serve as the sub-class d field check. Suit must say which. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: answered by Suit SE-27 and SE-28 — the load cue is breath with a load signature, and the HEAVY back-frame is on the Graph's closed consequence-channel list, so it is not module-body; see IDB-21.)*
83	
84	**Reference techniques, taken precisely.**
85	
86	| Reference | Adopt (exact technique) | Reject (exact technique, and why) |
87	|---|---|---|
88	| Project Zomboid [CON:357] | Items are physical objects whose condition persists when moved; "we keep it running" is the base-building feeling; death is lethal and the world goes on (user decision) | Weight-scaled encumbrance that slows movement (conflicts with the locked single `V_CARRY` and `NOISE_PER_TICK` carry). A container screen with weight totals and capacity (no pack capacity in the MVP). Tool durability that breaks tools. Crafting recipes and recipe magazines (anti-pillar) |
89	| Satisfactory [CON:358] | A machine shows it works through its moving part and medium; a def's ports define what it fits, with no partial fit | Recipes, build-from-materials and tiered unlock; throughput scale-up. The word `tier` means power priority only |
90	| Oxygen Not Included [CON:361] | Stored quantities are real physical stock with exact conservation [LSG:203] | A build menu that materialises a machine from raw material — salvage is the only faucet |
91	| Barotrauma [CON:360] | Co-op hauling of physical items between hulls | Fabricators, deconstructors and outpost shops; weapon item stats |
92	| Pandorum [CON:364] | The hands-free chest lamp: the beam stays available while carrying; a carried module rides above the helmet and never covers the chest point [ART:512] | Any flashlight-as-held-item def — the lamp is not an item def |
93	| Beyond the Aquila Rift [CON:363] | "The kindness of the lie": phantom salvage is the lie that feels like relief, and the weight is the unkind truth | A lie with no check [CON:267-268] |
94	| Alien: Isolation (not in the concept's list; flagged as an added reference) | A scarce thrown light that changes what can be seen and what can see you: `cons_glowstick` is a pool that counts as exposure [ART:286] | Flares or noisemakers as lures with damage-adjacent effects — tool effects belong to Attention and Horror, not the def |
95	| Loot-driven action games (anti-reference) | — | Rarity colours, affixes, item level and "legendary" tiers; violet and flesh are reserved for sanity leaks [CON:333-334], so no rarity hue may use them |
96	
97	**Anti-pillar guard rails this GDD states (concept wording, each with a lint).**
98	
99	| ID | Anti-pillar [CON:285-298] | Guard rail in the Item DB | Lint or review hook |
100	|---|---|---|---|
101	| AP-1 | "NOT a freeform ship-building sandbox: welding is functional and modules are pre-shaped." | A def fixes `node_kind`, `ports[]` and its cell; none is editable, combinable or rotatable into a new shape; one def is one Graph node. No composite module | (lint) no def has `recipe`, `ingredients`, `craft*`, `build_cost` or `editable` |
102	| AP-2 | "NOT a combat game: no weapon tree. Tools may repel or distract ... nothing levels up from killing" | Tools list verbs only; the only charge-bearing def, `tool_suppressant`, is dormant and outside the MVP roster (X6), and any repel or distract effect is Attention's and Horror's *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | (lint) no def has `damage`, `accuracy`, `armour`, `dps`, `xp` or `unlock` |
103	| AP-3 | No shop, no crafting; salvage is the only faucet (index brief, P5) | `salvage_yield` is the only function that turns a world event into an `ItemInstance`, beside authored placements; no currency exists | (lint) no `price`, `value_gold`, `sell`, `buy` or `vendor`; the registry `items:` entry never fills `value_gold` |
104	| AP-4 | "NOT intentional PvP" | No def has a friendly-harm or crewmate-targeting field | (review) no def field references another player |
105	| AP-5 | "NOT an authored linear story: no chapters or cutscenes; lore is found and assembled." | `curio_data_core` is a thing with mass and no behaviour in the MVP; its content is the Knowledge Codex's | (lint) no `quest`, `story_flag` or `lore_text` field; display text is a key only |
106	| AP-6 | Tone [CON:327-334; ART 6.2] | Display names are technician-plain nouns in the manufacturer's register ("scrubber", "battery cell", "pipe fitting"); no value adjectives, no flesh or organic naming despite the design metaphor. # Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

</system-reminder>

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience

4. Formulas — all math defined with variables

7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

111	### Core Rules
112	
113	*Every rule below is a data-contract rule of the Item DB module (`src/data/items/` in the code root — location is an ADR candidate), stated so an implementer can write it and a tester can falsify it. Rules are `IDB-n`, numbered and named, as the Graph's LS-n and the kernel's CR-n are. Graph- and registry-sourced numbers are written by their locked name with a `[LSG:n]`/`[REG:n]` tag and appear once; every number this GDD introduces is tagged **[PH]** and is a registry candidate (Section G). Where a rule records an alternative that was considered and rejected, the rejection is part of the rule: a later change must answer it. Examples use only roster `def_id`s (IDB-31) or are marked "illustrative, not in the catalogue", because an example in a GDD is read as a contract.*
114	
115	**IDB-1 — The Item DB is a static, immutable catalogue.** It defines what a thing *is* (mass, ports, ratings, repair part, yield) and what it *fits* (port types, node kind, carry class); nothing on a def says what it is *worth*. It registers **no kernel state block, no step hook, no command and no mutator** — consistent with the kernel's Interactions table (KRN:190-206) having no Item DB row and with CR-6 freezing the block registry at the end of BOOTING [KRN:98]. It is loaded once in BOOTING into an `ItemCatalog`, scene-tree free (kernel H10), read-only afterwards, constructed as `ItemCatalog.new(data, graph_tables)` with both inputs injected and no static, singleton or autoload state (so catalogue tests can build many catalogues in one process; IDB-26) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, and callable from `validate`, from P3 and from presentation, because every query in IDB-28 is pure. It **rejects nothing**: every rejection reason that concerns an item (`BUSY`, `OUT_OF_CHARGES`, `PORT_INCOMPAT`, `NOT_REPAIRABLE`) belongs to Interaction, Suit or the Graph. *Alternative considered:* one WORLD block `items.state` owning every instance with its own id counter — rejected: it duplicates Suit's carried-module state (the index gives Suit "carried modules" [IDX:27]), adds a write path every neighbour must call, and contradicts the producer's advice to keep this system thin and data-shaped [IDX:143]. *Alternative considered:* a hybrid catalogue plus a small `items.loose` block — rejected: it invents ownership the neighbours may not want; the loose-world holder is an Open Question, not a decision made here (IDB-16).
116	
117	**IDB-2 — Six def classes, one prefix and one numeric range each.** Every def belongs to exactly one class, named by its `def_id` prefix and bounded by its `type_id` range; the class fixes the default carry class.
118	
119	| Class | `def_id` prefix | `type_id` range | Default `carry_class` | MVP count | Meaning |
120	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
121	| Module | `mod_` | 1000-1999 | `CARRIED` | 13 | One Graph node (IDB-6); installed, salvaged, patched, repaired |
122	| Tool | `tool_` | 2000-2999 | `HAND` | 3 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: was 4; `tool_suppressant` is dormant, X6)* | A hand-rail tool; never consumed (IDB-11) |
123	| Consumable | `cons_` | 3000-3999 | `STOWED` | 1 | A counted item spent on use (IDB-12) |
124	| Part | `part_` | 4000-4999 | `STOWED` | 5 | Consumed by a full repair (IDB-13) |
125	| Curio | `curio_` | 5000-5999 | `CARRIED` | 1 | Mass with no Graph presence (IDB-14) |
126	| Junk | `junk_` | 9000-9999 | `CARRIED` | 0 (reserved, vertical slice) | A true-mass decoy for phantom salvage (IDB-22) |
127	
128	`CARRIED` means the instance occupies the single `controller.state.carry_ref` [PCI:131, PC-8]; `HAND` means it occupies the hand rail; `STOWED` means it is a counted entry in the Suit's block. The Item DB defines the class; Suit and the Controller own the slots (IDB-16). Capacity is 999 `type_id`s per class (a boot assertion): the class base (1000, 2000, ... 9000) is reserved and never assigned, so the usable range is base+1 to base+999 (orchestrator ruling, QA B8; F-8 and AC-73 pin it). The classes are fixed in the MVP; a seventh class would need a new prefix, a new range and a `catalogue_version` bump (IDB-27).
129	
130	**IDB-3 — Two keys: `def_id` persists, `type_id` stays in memory.** `def_id` is a lowercase ASCII snake_case string `<class>_<family>[_<variant>]`, at most `ID_MAX_LEN` 40 characters [PH], matching `^(mod|tool|cons|part|curio|junk)_[a-z][a-z0-9]*(_[a-z0-9]+)*$` (digits are legal after the first letter: `mod_o2_tank` is a roster id). `type_id` is an unsigned 16-bit integer, append-only, never reused. **Only `def_id` ever reaches a save, a snapshot, a `SalvageRecord`, a hash or a replicated record**; `type_id` exists for in-memory tables and the vertical slice's replication summaries, so renumbering can never break a save. This mirrors the Graph's own contract: "`def_id` is a string and type ids are numbers" [LSG:832], with stable content type IDs under ADR-LSG-08 [LSG:26]. A dialect is a separate field, never an id token (IDB-23). A rename after release is an alias, not a new id (IDB-27). *Alternative considered:* a string key only (no compact in-memory key, nothing to bound a typo) and a numeric key only (contradicts the Graph's string-in-saves rule) — both rejected; the pair is kept in step by the bijection assertion of IDB-4.
131	
132	**IDB-4 — The id ledger and the boot assertions.** A committed ledger `assets/data/items/ids.lock.json` lists every `(def_id, type_id)` pair ever shipped and the `retired_ids[]`. Boot refuses the build with `ITEM_BOOT_TYPE_ID(class, id)`, by analogy to `GRAPH_BOOT_TYPE_ID(table, id)` [LSG:1037], when any of these holds: two defs share a `type_id`; a `type_id` lies outside its class range; a `def_id` prefix disagrees with its class; a `type_id` is in `retired_ids`; a shipped `def_id` appears in the ledger with a different `type_id`; or a ledger pair is missing from the catalogue without a `retired_ids` entry or a `dormant` marker *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Formula F-8 is the assertion. **Dormant entries** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: a ledger pair may carry `dormant: true`, meaning the def is cut from the current build but its interface may return (X6). A dormant pair need not be in the catalogue, no other def may take its `def_id` or its `type_id`, and it may be re-shipped only unchanged (same pair). A dormant pair was never shipped to a save, so it needs no `renamed_from`. At MVP the only dormant entry is `tool_suppressant` 2004; it is distinct from `retired_ids`, which are never reused. Aliases (`renamed_from[]`, IDB-27) are resolved transitively to a depth of at most `ALIAS_DEPTH_MAX` 8 [PH]; a cycle, a self-alias, or an alias equal to a live `def_id` refuses to boot (`ITEM_BOOT_ALIAS(def_id)`), because an alias never creates a def and a retired string reused for a different def would let an old save silently load the wrong thing. The sim never iterates a Dictionary [LSG:64, LS-1 (i)]: the catalogue exposes arrays sorted ascending by `type_id` (`defs_of_class`), and a `def_id`-keyed map is for lookup only.

134	**IDB-5 — Fields every def carries.**

A module sheet (`mach_<name>`) names its frames by the state tokens `running`, `stopped`, `whole`, `cracked` and, for a lamp, the pair `lit` / `unlit` (In-World Instruments IW-17); the def lists the tokens its sheet draws in `sprite_states` |

146	| `cell` | enum | `M96` (96x96, 2x2 tiles), `P48`, `P48x96`, `P96x48`, `T80` (80x80 tool and overlay) | Sprite cell class [ART:1013-1055, 8.2] |

156	
157	*Forbidden keys (lint).* A def has **no** field named `damage`, `accuracy`, `armour`, `range`, `durability`, `dps`, `xp`, `unlock`, `price`, `value`, `value_gold`, `sell`, `buy`, `cost`, `vendor`, `shop`, `recipe`, `ingredients`, `craft*`, `build_cost`, `editable`, `rarity_weight`, `drop_rate`, `set_bonus`, `win`, `escape`, `quest`, `story_flag`, `lore_text`, `appears_as`, `displayed_as`, `fake_mass`, `lure_sprite` or `hallucination_*`, and no key that makes one item produce another (the single exception is the `repair_part_id` to scrap-yield link of IDB-17). Stock is a Graph node field, not an `ItemInstance` field, so the Graph owns the behaviour; this GDD states the **binding requirement** on it: on restore, the excess above the live cap moves to the section's `discarded_*` counter (conserved, so the conservation sum closes) and is **logged** (a diagnostic naming the node, the old stock and the cap); it is never a refusal and never silent. Rationale: the Graph's `GRAPH_RESTORE_OUT_OF_RANGE` treats a value above its documented max as a hard failure, which would brick every saved game on a downward retune; the world must lose the excess the way it loses stock at a cut, by a conserved, visible rule. This is routed to the Graph owner (Open Question 31) and tested by AC-105, BLOCKED-ON the Graph. (b) **`cap_bp` against a retuned `PATCH_CAP_BP`.** The patched-module invariant is `cap_bp < HP_FULL` with no tie to the current `PATCH_CAP_BP` (IDB-15), so a saved `cap_bp` 6000 restores and reinstalls at 6000 even after `PATCH_CAP_BP` is retuned to 5500; the next PATCH takes `min(hp_cap, PATCH_CAP_BP)` (LS-23), and a PATCH on `hp` at or above the new cap is refused `ABOVE_PATCH_CAP` with `hp` never clamped down (M7). The Item DB never rewrites a saved cap. AC-106 tests it.

Every row carries the tag **[DECL] declared here; Graph validates at load**. Port-type ids are the Graph's LS-4 numbers, cited by number and never redefined. The rule below, formerly "provisional" and routed as Open Question 10, is the Item DB's settled statement of what those two mutators now guarantee, and no AC waits on a ruling.)* The Graph's signatures are locked and are not restated or edited here; the Item DB states: (i) **stored quantities** — BATTERY `stock`, O2_TANK `stock`, RESERVOIR `stock_ml` and FUEL_TANK `stock_ml` — are **discarded into the section's `discarded_*` counters on salvage**, conserved the way `discard_section` (M4 [LSG:183]) conserves [LSG:799], and a reinstalled store starts at stock 0 (the Graph's own conservation note lists M5 among the only mutators that create a Graph quantity [LSG:799]; stock 0 creates none, so the invariant stays trivial); (ii) **patch state persists through salvage.** A module cut out and put back is the same body with the same history: a reinstalled module gets `hp = SalvageRecord.hp`; a module whose `hp_cap` was `PATCH_CAP_BP` reinstalls **capped** at it and **carries its decay clock** (`patched_at_step` unchanged); an un-patched module reinstalls at `hp_cap = HP_FULL` with no clock (the fresh-node default [LSG:68]). Only a FULL repair, which spends a part (IDB-20 (6)), lifts a cap; no cut and reinstall does. **The launder is closed by rule, not by a tripwire, and only while every holder keeps all six instance fields** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, BLOCKING: Interaction's IA-28 `loose[]` then stored a single `condition` number, so a drop lost `cap_bp` and `patched_at_step` and a pickup returned a clean module; the rule is closed on the Item DB and Graph side (M5/M6) and *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* closed at the Interaction holder by IA-28, and the regression proof is AC-117)*: a free, repeatable action must not stand in for the finite part (the Player Fantasy design test), and the bolted patch plate keeps its meaning after the module has been cut out and put back (Pillar 1, physical history; Pillar 5). **Mechanism (settled; was the routed CONFLICT).** The record carries `hp_cap` and `patched_at_step` (M6) and the reinstall restores them through M5's `hp_cap` and `patched_at_step` arguments, so Assembly's `install_module` passes the instance's `cap_bp` and `patched_at_step` straight through with `hp_start := condition_bp`; the Item DB extends no Graph mutator and edits no Graph value. The Graph's Open Question was answered by the amendment itself (LS-18 M5/M6), not by a separate ruling. **The clock is absolute and time in transit counts:** `patched_at_step` is the Graph's `step_no`, copied unchanged, and the Graph's wear terms apply only to subjects in the graph [LSG:505, 769], so transit never costs `hp`; but a module carried or shelved longer than `PATCH_DECAY_S` 240 s reinstalls already past its hold and starts to decay at the next wear period. A shelf is not a pause button. `hp` is the damage and carries unchanged. The cut still costs real time, noise and air, so a salvage is never a free action: the SEVERED stubs leak at `OPEN_END_RATE_PM` until `cap_port` [LSG:772], the island re-solves with the module gone [LSG:773], the carry runs at `V_CARRY` 1 and the module stays DEGRADED at `eff` 750 until a part is spent. The control is the rule itself plus the split persistence tests (AC-32a to AC-32f), and any build in which a reinstall resets a cap or a clock reopens this rule *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the F-15 break-even and its `T_CYCLE_MIN` tripwire are withdrawn as blocking items; they compared one salvage cycle against the whole patch chore over a horizon, which are not comparable, and the persistence tests are the real control)*. **Stock is in situ, not hauled:** O2 is regenerated by the scrubber, charge by the reactor at `CH_CAP`, and coolant circulates rather than being consumed; **fuel is the exception** — it is finite and non-renewable ("nothing the Graph does refills the fuel tank or the O2 tank" [LSG:793]) — so fuel reaches the home-ship by welding a derelict section whose tank joins the loop, not by hauling a tank, and the MVP roster has no fuel-canister def. The patch-state rule (ii) and the stored-quantity rule (i) are now guaranteed by the Graph's own M5 and M6 text (Open Question 10 closed). A reinstalled empty store must read as empty in the world (a dark store, a silent gauge on the sane channel), or it reads as the game cheating — a note for the presentation systems. **A saved `cap_bp` is never re-based:** a patched module whose `cap_bp` was recorded under an older `PATCH_CAP_BP` reinstalls at the recorded value even if that constant was retuned since (IDB-15, "Restore against a retuned catalogue"), and the next PATCH takes `min(hp_cap, PATCH_CAP_BP)`.
337	
338	**Runtime fields on reinstall: reset or carry** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; the review asked what reinstall does to the other node fields, and warned that resetting them is itself a free "fix" of the same shape as the launder).* M5's signature passes only `hp_start`, `hp_cap` and `patched_at_step`, so every other field of the new node takes the Graph's fresh-node default. The rule that decides whether that is acceptable: **physical history persists, environment and switch state does not.** A field persists if it is damage or wear (`hp`, `hp_cap`, `patched_at_step`); a field resets if it is derived from `hp` and so recomputed (it cannot be a free fix because the cause is carried), a switch or setpoint the player chose (not history), or a transient whose cause lives in the old room.
339	
340	| Runtime field (LS-3) | On reinstall | Why this is not a free fix |
341	|---|---|---|
342	| `hp`, `hp_cap`, `patched_at_step` | **carried** (M5 arguments) | the damage and the patch history are the module's body |
343	| `state`, `forced_mode`, `forced_mode_next`, `fail_since_step`, `warn_since_step` | reset, then **re-derived from `hp`** by the next Graph run | a module below `HP_FAIL` is FAILED again at the next run; the cause (`hp`) is carried, so no failure is cleared that `hp` did not already clear. A forced mode caused by a hazard in the old room (overheat, short) re-fires only if the new room produces it |
344	| REACTOR `scram`, `starve_steps`, `out_w`, `fuel_rem` | reset (cold, unfuelled, ramping from 0) | a reactor cut out is cold; a SCRAM is a latched trip whose cause (overheat, no fuel) is the old room's and re-trips in a room that causes it. This is a **switch-state reset, not a repair**: it does not raise `hp` |
345	| CABLE_JUNCTION `breaker_closed` | the Graph's fresh default | a breaker position is a switch; the damage that tripped it is `hp`, which is carried |
346	| PUMP `throttle_pm`, VENT `setpoint_pp` | fresh default | player settings, not history |
347	| LOAD `energised_at_step` | reset | the inrush window restarts at install; the first re-energise carries the inrush (V3's cost) |
348	| RESERVOIR `t_cool`, `tc_rem` | reset to the loop's ambient | thermal state is equilibrated by the new room |

362	A reinstalled O2 tank, reservoir or fuel tank is therefore **a part of the structure, not a supply**: the MVP gives no way to fill it, which is stated here so no author places one expecting a refill (Open Question 37).
363	
364	**IDB-19 — Repair parts: `repair_part_for` and `parts_per_full`.** The pure lookup `repair_part_for(subject_kind, kind_id, loop) -> (part_def_id, count)` (F-3) returns a part and a count, or `NONE`. It exists because the Graph says a full repair "requires the Item DB part named by the subject's `def_id`" [LSG:222] while edges carry no `def_id` [LSG:72], and two of the eight MVP faults — the coolant leak on a PIPE and the oxygen pinhole on a DUCT [LSG:228] — are edges. The lookup is **total over the five `subject_kind` values** of the Graph's M7 enum, NODE 1 / EDGE 2 / COMPARTMENT 3 / SEAM 4 / OPENING 5 [LSG:150], so it answers for whatever M7 is handed. Resolution order: (1) a NODE with a non-empty `def_id` uses that def's `repair_part_id` and `parts_per_full`; (2) a NODE with an empty `def_id` (HULL_SEGMENT) uses the node-kind row; (3) an EDGE uses `(edge_kind, loop)`, including the SEAM loop sub-edge (kind 6) mapped to that loop's line part; (4) COMPARTMENT (3), SEAM (4) and OPENING (5) return `NONE`, as do the node kinds 1, 2 and the vertical-slice kinds with no part. `NONE` is defined in IDB-20. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the formerly routed wording conflict is closed; LS-23 and M7 now read "named by `repair_part_for(subject)`".)*
365	
366	| Subject | Key | Part | Count |
367	|---|---|---|---|
368	| NODE with a def | `def.repair_part_id` | per def (below) | `def.parts_per_full` |
369	| NODE 50 HULL_SEGMENT (no def) | node kind | `part_hull_plate` | 1 |
370	| EDGE 1 DUCT | edge kind | `part_duct_coupling` | 1 |
371	| EDGE 2 CABLE | edge kind | `part_cable_splice` | 1 |
372	| EDGE 3 PIPE on loop 3 or 4 | edge kind + loop | `part_pipe_fitting` | 1 |
373	| EDGE 5 VALVE | edge kind + loop | loop 1 `part_duct_coupling`; loop 3 or 4 `part_pipe_fitting` | 1 |
374	| EDGE 6 SEAM (a loop edge crossing sections) | edge kind + loop | the part of that loop's line (as DUCT, CABLE or PIPE above) | 1 |
375	| EDGE 4 STRUT (vertical slice) | edge kind | `part_hull_plate` | 1 |
376	| SEAM record (`SeamRecord`; `q`, `leak_bp`) | subject kind | `NONE` in the MVP | 0 |
377	| EDGE 7 OPENING; NODE 1, 2; vertical-slice node kinds 34, 42, 51 | — | `NONE` | 0 |
378	
379	*Per-def parts.* Machine defs — `mod_scrubber`, `mod_reactor_cell`, `mod_battery_cell`, `mod_coolant_pump`, `mod_radiator`, `mod_coolant_reservoir`, `mod_o2_tank`, `mod_fuel_tank`, `mod_vent`, `mod_heater` — name `part_machine_kit`; `mod_breaker_junction`, `mod_lamp` and `mod_door_motor` name `part_cable_splice` (electrical fixtures, not machines; this refines the ruling's "every machine node kind"). `parts_per_full` is 1 except `mod_reactor_cell`, which is 2 [PH] (the heart of the ship costs twice). `scrap_count` is 1 on every module def (IDB-17). A DESTROYED subject takes no part because it is never repairable (`NOT_REPAIRABLE` [LSG:771]). `PATCH_CAP_BP` stays 6000 [REG:6021-6037]; its build rule is the Graph's, quoted: `PATCH_CAP_BP` "must be >= `LEAK_HP` + one wear period and < `HP_OK`" [LSG:903], where one wear period is `PATCH_DECAY_BP_PER_100` 100 bp [LSG:769] — never restated here as a number. (orchestrator ruling: on the SEAM rows the specialists split three ways — the game-designer maps a seam to the hull plate, the systems-designer resolves seam sub-edges per loop with the `SeamRecord` unmapped, the economy-designer leaves the record to Assembly's weld; this rule takes the systems form; the Graph has since ruled that a FULL on `subject_kind` SEAM 4 is not offered at MVP (LS-18 M7; `repair_part_for` NONE), so the held `NONE` is confirmed *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. On tanks and reservoirs the economy-designer's plumbing-part mapping is dropped in favour of the machine kit, keeping the kit the scarce part and the family count at five.)
380	
381	**IDB-20 — Part consumption economics (Interaction designed: IA-18 discharges these statements).** The Item DB owns `parts_per_full`, so it states the economic rule; Interaction owns the command, the channel timing and the state that implements it. (1) **One part-count per job.** A full repair job is one accepted `begin_patch(FULL)`; its cost is `parts_per_full` of `repair_part_for(subject)`, consumed at the **first productive channel step** — the first step in which `hp_cap` or `hp` rises (registry: `full_job_charge`, Interaction's: the part is RESERVED at the Applied FULL begin tick, so the actor's visible stock falls then, and is released, with no timer, if the channel ends early with no credited block or on an OUTCOME; `FULL_CHANNEL_TICKS` is the hold length only; it is PAID, i.e. spent for good, at the first productive step, and at any cancel, abort or restore once a block is credited) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*. A full repair on a subject with `hp_cap = HP_FULL` and `hp = hp_cap` consumes nothing and resolves `PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR)` (Interaction IA-18 statement 7, an Applied-and-did-nothing outcome). (2) **A full job issues only `kind = FULL` steps**: a PATCH step inside a paid job would re-cap `hp_cap` to `PATCH_CAP_BP` and waste the part [LSG:186]. (3) **No refund on interruption**: the part is spent, and the `hp` already applied stays (steps are real). (4) **Recommendation to Interaction (not an Item DB rule or knob)**: a resume allowance for a re-issued `begin_patch(FULL)` on the same subject shortly after an interruption (adopted: Interaction's `FULL_JOB_GRACE_S` 60 s [PLACEHOLDER], IA-18 statement 6, for the same seat on the same subject; other seats are charged), so a stagger or a pod hop does not double-charge a part. (5) **A PATCH never consumes a part** [REG:6033]; **no patch-kit def exists** in the roster, and a PATCH consumes no item at all [REG:6033; LSG:222] — the Graph has removed the former "patch kits are the Item DB's finite consumable" wording, so LS-23, M7 and the registry now agree; a PATCH on a subject whose `hp` is at or above `PATCH_CAP_BP` is refused by the Graph as `ABOVE_PATCH_CAP` and `hp` is **never clamped down** (LS-18 M7), so Interaction offers only FULL there *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: Open Questions 9 and 14 (patch kits) closed on those rule ids)*. (6) **Wear is a full repair**: a duty-worn machine at 6900 `hp` with `hp_cap` 10000 can only be raised above `PATCH_CAP_BP` by a full repair, which is the engine of Pillar 5 — the part is what wear costs. (7) In co-op, each player's part is consumed only if that player's first step is applied; a second seat beginning on a subject already under a job is `BUSY` at `validate` and makes no reservation (Interaction IA-34). (8) A missing part produces no `BLOCKED` and no reject: FULL is simply not offered without `parts_per_full` of the part (Interaction IA-18 statement 1); the Item DB rejects nothing. (9) **`NONE` means Interaction offers no FULL job on that subject** (PATCH only); a FULL repair never costs zero parts, so a subject whose `repair_part_for` is `NONE` cannot have its `hp_cap` restored for free. The SEAM record (subject_kind 4) is held at `NONE`, which the Graph confirmed: a FULL on `subject_kind` SEAM 4 is not offered at MVP (LS-18 M7) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; Open Question 12 closed)*. The weld that makes a seam is V9 (MVP); V11 SEAL_SEAM, which sets a seam's `leak_bp` to 0, is vertical slice A [LSG:228, 648].
382	
383	**IDB-21 — Weight: true integer grams, a class, and a body cue — never speed or noise.** `mass_g` is an integer (the Graph's pattern is scaled integers: mGU, mC, dkPa, µmL [LSG:64]). `weight_class` (F-1) is LIGHT, MEDIUM or HEAVY by two thresholds `WEIGHT_MEDIUM_G` 5000 and `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` 25000 [PH]. The Item DB supplies the true number; **Suit turns carried (and stowed) mass into a consequence-channel body cue** — breath, strain; never a number on screen — and the class is the resolution that cue must at least have. Mass does **not** change `V_CARRY` (1 base px/tick, one constant [REG:5338-5356]) or the carry `NOISE_PER_TICK` (1 [REG:5442-5457]); the Controller already makes the carry visibly slow ("a module at chest height halves the walk" [PCI:98]), and the haul cost of a module is its distance and the single `carry_ref`, not its mass (F-13 is the worked comparison: a 90 kg reactor cell and a 6 kg data core cost the same per tile); a stowed HEAVY item adds one class-keyed rule, the run disable of IDB-13, never a grams term *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. **There is no pack capacity and no weight readout in the MVP**: weight matters for the single carried module, the hull plate and the field check. **BINDING on Suit & Equipment (a requirement, not a courtesy): stowed mass counts, not only the carried module.** When `stowed_mass_g` (F-2: the sum of `instance_mass_g` over the holder's STOWED instances) is at or above `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G`, the Suit must produce a closed-list consequence-channel body cue (breath, visor fog, rime or shiver, from Suit's SE-27 set, no vignette; the Suit chooses which, it may not choose none and may not choose a module-body cue). The MVP case is the 30 kg `part_hull_plate`, the heaviest object a player can hold: a design in which it has no world footprint, or costs the hauler nothing the body can report, makes the exposure cost of hauling it avoidable and weakens "the physical world is ground truth" (Pillars 1 and 3). **It is also seen, derived and not authored:** a STOWED def at `weight_class` HEAVY draws a back-frame sprite (a plate on the back rig) that never covers the chest point, the per-facing beam origin [ART:512]; there is no new def field, the rule is the class (and `stack_max` 1, above). The sprite keys on a stowed def's own `weight_class` and the body cue on the summed `stowed_mass_g`; they are two readings of one rule and in the MVP roster only the hull plate crosses `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` either way. The body cue is the truthful report and is the sub-class d field check. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier sentence "the sprite is module-body channel and may lie" is out of date. Suit's conflict C1 was closed on 2026-10-27: the HEAVY back-frame is on the Graph's closed consequence-channel list (SE-27; registry `truth_channel_union`), so for a stowed HEAVY item the plate on the back is a non-corruptible visual as well as a breath cue. The inspect card and any other module-body surface may still lie. The MEDIUM class has no such visual; see the accessibility clause below.)* Whether a stowed haul adds carry-rate noise is Interaction's open choice (OQ-4); any such term is flat per tile and keyed to the class, never a function of grams, so the locked `NOISE_PER_TICK` carry value and the rule above stay true. Channel split: the body cue is consequence-channel and never corruptible; the sprite and the inspect card are module-body and may lie [LSG:44]. Boundary hazard: a def sitting exactly on a threshold flips class on a 1 g edit, so the lint `WEIGHT_CLASS_MARGIN_PM` (default 100 permille [PH]) keeps every def at least that far from both thresholds (the forbidden bands are 4500-5500 g and 22500-27500 g at the defaults) and is **blocking in CI**; a boundary value is a defect, not a class-population argument. Every roster mass clears both bands (`mod_battery_cell` is 22000 g, MEDIUM; the nearest others are `tool_welder` 4000 g and `mod_vent` 6000 g).
384	
385	*Weight-system clauses added by the design review* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. (1) **Feasible windows (published, and computed by the lint).** Against the shipped masses and the blocking margin lint, the thresholds are not free across their old knob ranges. `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` must keep `part_hull_plate` (30000 g, and `mod_coolant_pump` 30000 g) HEAVY with margin, so `30000 - H >= H x margin / 1000`, and `mod_battery_cell` (22000 g) MEDIUM with margin, so `H - 22000 >= H x margin / 1000`: at the default margin 100 the window is **24,445 to 27,272 g** (at the old range top of 40000 the plate silently stops being HEAVY). `WEIGHT_MEDIUM_G` must keep `tool_welder` (4000 g) LIGHT and `mod_vent` and `curio_data_core` (6000 g) MEDIUM with margin: **4,445 to 5,454 g**. `WEIGHT_CLASS_MARGIN_PM` is feasible only up to **150** (the window for `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` closes between 150 and 160, and is 25,883 to 26,086 g at 150); the old range top of 200 is infeasible with this roster. The lint computes these windows from the roster and prints them; a knob outside its window fails the build, and a roster mass edit shifts them. (2) **Roster-semantic lint (blocking).** The plate is HEAVY, and no other STOWED def is HEAVY; the heaviest full stack of ordinary stowed parts at the shipped `stack_max` values (4 duct couplings, 4 cable splices, 4 pipe fittings, 2 machine kits, 4 glowsticks = 15,200 g) stays below `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G`, so no legal `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` value lets an ordinary stack reach HEAVY at those `stack_max` values; `stack_max` is itself a knob (1-8), so a `stack_max` edit re-runs the lint. (3) **Suit's masking and exclusion, acknowledged.** Suit's SE-28 reads `cue_load = max(carried_class, stowed_class)`, so a stowed plate masks a carried module's class and the Vertical Slice lift-and-weigh check is blind to a carried item while the plate is on the back (Suit OQ-8); SE-41 excludes parts reserved by a FULL job from `stowed_mass_g` (F-2). Both are Suit's rules and are cited, not restated. States row 14 is what restores the check (shed the plate first). (4) **Hysteresis (requested of Suit).** The stowed-sum class has no margin: a 200 g glowstick can flip `stowed_class` at the edge, so the cue needs enter/exit hysteresis (enter at `WEIGHT_*_G`, exit below it by `WEIGHT_CLASS_MARGIN_PM`); the cue is Suit's, so this is a binding ask, Open Question 35. (5) **Calibration (requested of Boarding and Suit).** Three classes carry little information without a reference: the first sortie must give the player a calibrating carry of a MEDIUM and a HEAVY item before any lure can appear (Boarding's reference carry `htr_a` is MEDIUM; the plate is HEAVY), Open Question 35. (6) **Accessibility of the sole mass channel.** The weight check is audio-first (breath), which is a gap for a deaf or hard-of-hearing player (Boarding OQ-BS-21). For HEAVY the back-frame already supplies a paired visual on the closed consequence list; MEDIUM has none. This GDD requires that any further visual cadence for the load (a visor fog or rime variant) be placed on the closed list by Suit and the Perception Filter, because a visual that is not on the list can be corrupted and so becomes lie-able (Pillar 1); otherwise `design/accessibility-requirements.md` must record an explicit exception. The accessibility file does not exist yet; this GDD does not block another system's story on it (Open Question 40), but the Vertical Slice phantom-salvage story depends on the answer. *Alternatives considered:* weight shown only on the inspect card (corruptible, fails the field check); a second instrument such as a pod scale (reserved for the vertical slice); weight scaling noise (conflicts with the locked carry noise for heavy modules) — rejected or deferred.
386	
387	**IDB-22 — Phantom-salvage support (hallucination sub-class d): a true mass on every def, and off-band junk.** The Item DB supplies exactly two things to sub-class d: a **true `mass_g` on every def**, and the existence of `junk_` defs. A junk def's `mass_g` differs from the mass of the lure it will be dressed as by at least `WEIGHT_TELL_MIN_PM` 300 permille [PH] (F-10), **and** the two fall in different `weight_class` values — because the Suit's cue resolves classes, not grams, a 30 percent gap inside one class gives the same cue and the check could not fail the lie (Suit's cue ladder is three steps, LIGHT, MEDIUM, HEAVY, SE-28, so the class clause stands; if a later Suit ladder is finer the class clause is replaced by "differs by at least one cue step"). **SE-28 precondition** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the class check can fail a lie only while the carried item's class is what the cue reads; because Suit's `cue_load = max(carried_class, stowed_class)`, a seat whose stowed class is HEAVY (the plate on the back) is masked, and a junk-versus-lure comparison is valid only for a seat with no HEAVY stowed item (Sanity SN-21 already gives such a seat no lure); the player's way to remove the mask is the shed of States row 14. The lure sprite is the Perception Filter's to draw; the lure-band data and the lie belong to Sanity (SN-21); a def never carries a believed, displayed or fake value. The junk-tell lint (F-10) reads the Sanity-owned band file (registry: `lure_bands.json`; path `assets/data/sanity/lure_bands.json`, SN-21; `{band_id, mid_g, class}`, lint-only, never loaded at runtime or persisted). **No lure data lives under `assets/data/items/`**: the table of what a junk def is dressed as is the lie's data, so neither a junk def nor any file in the Item DB folder says what a thing will look like. The MVP uses the field for `weight_class` and the body cue only; junk defs ship in the vertical slice (reserved ids 9000-9999), and a junk def that fails F-10 is not releasable.
388	
389	**IDB-23 — Dialect is a skin, not a stat.** Defs carry `family` and `dialect`. A variant row may override stats, but **no MVP def does** (lint: every MVP def has `dialect: foundry` and no override), so no dominant dialect can emerge. `lattice` and `civil` are reserved enum values. The MVP derelicts are Foundry [IDX:31] and the home-ship's origin is Foundry [ART:298-330, 3.3]. Port *shape* (round, octagonal, rectangular) is sprite grammar and never a port-type id. A grafted section keeps its donor dialect, so a foreign module reads foreign and plays identically — the "foreign" read is a sprite concern. 428	Five economy rules follow. (1) **A patch is free of items; a part is an upgrade priced in scarcity.** A patch is free of items by locked design [REG:6033], so the part is never the *only* way to survive an MVP fault; it is the only way to stop *paying time* for it. That honest reading of Pillar 5 means **the MVP is always survivable with zero parts for a crew of N = 1: the patch treadmill is a playable, deliberately costly terminal state** (guarantee G-0, an authoring acceptance, **qualified per crew size N** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: "always survivable with zero parts" held only for N = 1 in a 1-to-4-player game; for N >= 2 one scrubber runs a deficit even fully repaired (F-14), so G-0 is "survivable for N = 1; for N >= 2 survivable only until the O2 tank empties unless a second scrubber is installed", and AC-42 is parameterised by N)*; it **holds by LS-10 and M7**: `FAILED` is repairable [LSG:125] and M7 rejects only DESTROYED [LSG:186], so a patch works on the broken breaker at `hp` 2000; the LS-26 phrase "dark until replaced" [LSG:228] is prose, routed to the Graph owner as a wording question, and one spare `mod_breaker_junction` placement is a recommendation to Derelict Authoring, not an Item DB guarantee): the terminal state when the parts are spent is the patch treadmill, and that state is designed as playable. It is a treadmill, not a farm: a patch decays (`PATCH_DECAY_S`), a patched scrubber holds one crew at margin zero, and with N >= 2 crew the treadmill loses ground (F-14: one scrubber, even fully repaired, runs a 200 mGU/step deficit at N = 2; holding N crew takes N patched scrubbers at margin zero and N times the re-patch chores), so zero-part survival is pressure and not a safe place to farm (the Pillar 5 design test). What makes the part worth hunting is quantified in F-14 (a patched scrubber at `PATCH_CAP_BP` makes exactly `R_BREATH` for one crew — margin zero — against a margin of +100 mGU/step for a fully repaired one, and the margin vanishes with a second crew). (2) **Part conservation: no verb converts parts.** `scrap_count` is exactly 1 on every module def in the MVP (boot-asserted), no def consumes a part to yield an item (no recycling, no upgrade), and the number of part instances in existence never exceeds the authored loose parts plus the DESTROYED module nodes. (3) **A supply ratio is an authoring target, not a runtime field.** The ratio of parts supplied to full-repair parts a diligent player could demand, `part_cover_pm` (F-11, now measured per part family and per reachable sortie set, in parts), is held in an advisory band of 500-800 permille [PH]; below it permanent fixes feel out of reach, above it every chronic fault is solved and nothing pushes inward. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: whether a per-family cover of 100 percent is intended is Open Question 38, resolved 2026-10-28 by delegated ruling G2.)* (orchestrator ruling: the three specialist proposals gave 750-1000, 500-750 and 500-800; the reconciled band is 500-800.) (4) **No placement without a consumer**: a module names an install target kind, a part a repair family, a consumable a `use_verb`, a tool its `verbs[]` — a def with no consumer in a placement table is the lint `PLACEMENT_NO_CONSUMER` (WARN; the data core, in the MVP). A lint fails any def or file under `assets/data/items/` that carries a forbidden key (IDB-5). (5) **Depth richness is expressed by placement, never by def stats (BINDING on Derelict Authoring and Depth Rings & Scarcity).** "Deeper Is Richer" is delivered through placement density, part supply (`part_cover_pm` by ring: F-11's band is the MVP default and Depth Rings may set a per-ring target) and authored `hp` (better-condition modules deeper). It is never delivered through def stats: no def carries a worth, dialect is a skin (IDB-23), and `grade` stays 0 and behaviourless; any future behaviour for `grade`, or any stat that differs by ring or dialect, requires a creative-director review before it enters a def.
