552	## Formulas
553	
554	All formulas are integer-only: the catalogue is data, and anything an instance carries into a holder block may be hashed or replicated (the kernel's `state_hash` and the Graph's LS-1 (b) rule), so no float is stored, hashed or compared. Truncation is floor, applied to non-negative operands only [LSG:64, LS-1 (d)]. Every duration is labelled **tick** (60 Hz, `TICK_RATE` 60) or **step** (the Graph's 10 Hz, `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6) or **s**. Formulas the Graph owns (D.4 `eff`, D.5 `out_scr`, D.14 `seam_at_weld`) are cited by name and line and never restated; where an example needs their value it says "evaluated by calling D.n". The ids F-1 to F-15 are those of IDB-32. Formulas F-1 to F-10 and F-12 are **runtime or boot** formulas; F-11, F-14 and F-15 are **design-time checks** (authoring and balance lints), and F-13 is a derivation that proves a rule by lock.
555	
556	### F-1 `weight_class`
557	
558	The weight_class formula is defined as:
559	
560	`weight_class(m) = LIGHT if m < WEIGHT_MEDIUM_G ; MEDIUM if WEIGHT_MEDIUM_G <= m < WEIGHT_HEAVY_G ; HEAVY if m >= WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` — and the blocking margin lint `margin_ok(m) = for T in {WEIGHT_MEDIUM_G, WEIGHT_HEAVY_G}: abs(m - T) * 1000 >= WEIGHT_CLASS_MARGIN_PM * T`
561	
562	**Variables:**
563	
564	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
565	|---|---|---|---|---|
566	| `m` | int g | 1..500000 | def `mass_g` (IDB-5) | True mass of one unit |
567	| `WEIGHT_MEDIUM_G` | int g | **feasible 4445-5454**, default 5000 (the old range 3000-8000 is infeasible against the roster under the blocking margin) | data [PH] ★ registry candidate | LIGHT/MEDIUM boundary *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
568	| `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` | int g | **feasible 24445-27272** at margin 100, default 25000 (the old range 15000-40000 let the plate silently stop being HEAVY at 40000 and let a full stack of ordinary parts, 15,200 g, reach HEAVY at 15000) | data [PH] ★ registry candidate | MEDIUM/HEAVY boundary *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
569	| `WEIGHT_CLASS_MARGIN_PM` | int permille | **50-150**, default 100 (200 is infeasible: the `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` window closes between 150 and 160) | data [PH] ★ registry candidate | Minimum relative distance of any def's mass from either threshold *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
570	
571	**Output Range:** one of three classes; `margin_ok` is a boolean. Boot assertion `WEIGHT_MEDIUM_G < WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` (`ITEM_BOOT_FIELD`). The margin lint is a blocking CI check (IDB-21), not a boot code. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the lint also computes and prints the feasible window of each threshold from the roster, and a roster-semantic lint asserts the plate is HEAVY and no other STOWED def is; the windows are derived in IDB-21 and are inputs to the registry ranges.)*
572	**Example:** `tool_cutter` 3500 g -> LIGHT (distance to 5000 is 1500 >= 5000 x 100 / 1000 = 500, pass). `curio_data_core` 6000 g -> MEDIUM (1000 >= 500, pass). `mod_battery_cell` 22000 g -> MEDIUM (distance to 25000 is 3000 >= 2500, pass; at the old 25000 g it sat exactly on the threshold, where the `>=` rule made it HEAVY and the lint failed). `mod_coolant_pump` 30000 g -> HEAVY (5000 >= 2500, pass). A def at 24000 g would fail the lint (1000 < 2500) and so cannot ship.
573	
574	### F-2 `instance_mass_g`
575	
576	The instance_mass_g formula is defined as:
577	
578	`instance_mass_g(inst) = mass_g(inst.def_id) * inst.count` ; `held_mass_g(holder) = sum of instance_mass_g over the holder's CARRIED, STOWED and IN_HAND instances` ; `stowed_mass_g(holder) = sum of instance_mass_g over the holder's STOWED instances` (the quantity the binding body cue of IDB-21 reads: `weight_class(stowed_mass_g)` HEAVY means the cue is owed; Suit counts **only the unreserved** count of a stack, because units RESERVED by a FULL job are out of the pack from the begin tick, SE-41, and Suit's `cue_load` also takes the max with the carried class and excludes in-hand tools, SE-28) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
579	
580	**Variables:**
581	
582	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
583	|---|---|---|---|---|
584	| `mass_g(def_id)` | int g | 1..500000 | catalogue | Per-unit true mass |
585	| `inst.count` | int | 1..`stack_max` | `ItemInstance` (IDB-15) | Stack size; 1 for modules, tools and curios |
586	
587	**Output Range:** 0..about 10^7 g (far below 2^53). Mass is **never persisted** on an instance (IDB-15); it is derived from the def on read, so a mass edit needs no migration.
588	**Example:** a player stows 4 `cons_glowstick` (200 g each = 800), 2 `part_pipe_fitting` (1200 g each = 2400) and 1 `part_machine_kit` (2000 g): `held_mass_g` = 800 + 2400 + 2000 = 5200 g; while also carrying a `mod_scrubber` (40000 g, count 1) it is 45200 g. The Suit turns the sum into a body cue (IDB-21); the Item DB supplies only the number. A player who stows one `part_hull_plate` (30000 g) has `stowed_mass_g` 30000, at or above `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` 25000, so the body cue is owed even though no module is carried.

591	
592	The repair_part_for formula is defined as:
593	
594	`repair_part_for(subject_kind, kind_id, loop) = (d.repair_part_id, d.parts_per_full) for NODE with def d ; (node_kind_part[kind_id], 1) for NODE with empty def_id ; (edge_part[(kind_id, loop)], 1) for EDGE ; (NONE, 0) for COMPARTMENT, SEAM, OPENING`

597

599	|---|---|---|---|---|
600	| `subject_kind` | enum | NODE 1, EDGE 2, COMPARTMENT 3, SEAM 4, OPENING 5 | Graph M7 [LSG:150, 186] | The function is total over all five values |
601	| `kind_id` | int | an LS-3 node-kind id or an LS-5 edge-kind id | Graph [LSG:68, 72] | Selects the row of IDB-19 |
602	| `loop` | int | 0..5 | Graph [LSG:66] | Needed for PIPE, VALVE and SEAM sub-edges |
603	| `d.repair_part_id` | string | a `part_` def | module def (IDB-19) | The part a module names |

607	**Example:** `mod_scrubber` node -> (`part_machine_kit`, 1); `mod_reactor_cell` node -> (`part_machine_kit`, 2); `mod_door_motor` node -> (`part_cable_splice`, 1); the oxygen pinhole DUCT (edge kind 1, loop 1) -> (`part_duct_coupling`, 1); the coolant-leak PIPE (kind 3, loop 3) -> (`part_pipe_fitting`, 1); the fuel-drip PIPE (kind 3, loop 4) -> (`part_pipe_fitting`, 1); a SEAM sub-edge of loop 3 (edge kind 6) -> (`part_pipe_fitting`, 1); HULL_SEGMENT (node kind 50) -> (`part_hull_plate`, 1); a COMPARTMENT, a `SeamRecord` (subject_kind 4) or an OPENING (subject_kind 5) -> (`NONE`, 0).

609	### F-4 `part_cost`
610	
611	The part_cost formula is defined as:
612	
613	`parts_consumed(job) = parts_per_full if the first productive channel step of an accepted FULL job is applied, else 0` ; `stock_after = stock_before - parts_consumed` ; permitted only if `stock_before >= parts_per_full` (Interaction's `validate`) ; `stock_visible = stock_before - parts_per_full` from the Applied FULL begin tick while the record is RESERVED or PAID (released, with no timer, if the channel ends early with no credited block or on an OUTCOME; registry: `full_job_charge`, Interaction's) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* ; `parts_consumed` above is the PAID amount
614	
615	**Variables:**
616	
617	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
618	|---|---|---|---|---|
619	| `parts_per_full` | int | 1..3 | F-3 | Cost of one full job |
620	| `stock_before` | int | 0..`stack_max` x stacks | holder (Suit's block) | Count of the required part def held |
621	| first productive step | event | — | Interaction | The first step in which `hp_cap` or `hp` rises (IDB-20) |

623	**Output Range:** `parts_consumed` is 0 for every PATCH [REG:6033], for a job rejected before its first applied step, and for a FULL on a subject already at `hp_cap` = `HP_FULL` with `hp` = `hp_cap` (`PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR)`); otherwise `parts_per_full`. A RESERVED part that is never PAID returns to the stock at `until`, so `parts_consumed` 0 can still show a visible dip for one channel. `stock_after >= 0` always.
624	**Example:** a FULL repair of the reactor (`parts_per_full` 2) with 3 `part_machine_kit` held (`stack_max` 2, so stacks of 2 and 1): from the Applied begin tick the visible stock reads 1 (2 kits RESERVED, `full_job_charge`); the first productive step pays them, leaving 1; with no credited block (an early end or an OUTCOME) they are released, with no timer. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* A PATCH on the same reactor spends 0. If the channel is interrupted after the first step the part stays spent and the raised `hp` stays (IDB-20 (3)).

626	### F-5 `salvage_yield`
627	
628	The salvage_yield formula is defined as:
629	
630	`salvage_yield(rec) = [] if rec.state in {ABSENT, SALVAGED} ; [ItemInstance(d.repair_part_id, d.scrap_count, 0, 0, 0, 0)] if rec.state = DESTROYED or rec.hp = 0 ; [ItemInstance(rec.def_id, 1, rec.hp, rec.hp_cap, patched_out, 0)] otherwise (rec.state in {OK, DEGRADED, FAILED} and rec.hp >= 1)` , where `d = def(rec.def_id)` and `patched_out := 0 if rec.hp_cap = HP_FULL else rec.patched_at_step` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, BLOCKING: the branch is keyed on `hp`, not on `state` alone, because the Graph lets a node sit FAILED at `hp` 0 while the warning gate is closed (Graph state-transition table, FAILED to DESTROYED row), and the old state-keyed form would have yielded a module at `condition_bp` 0, which IDB-15 and AC-82 refuse at restore. 793	| `NOISE_PER_TICK` | int | walk 1, carry 1, run 4 | registry [REG:5442-5457] (locked) | Attention units per tick *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
794	
795	**Output Range:** ticks 48..2880 for D 1..60 carrying; mass appears nowhere in the expression, which is the point: the Item DB cannot make a heavy thing slower or louder without a registry conflict. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: this expression covers the single carried module; Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: a stowed HEAVY item (the 30 kg plate) no longer costs nothing. Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): option (a) of D18, Open Question 32: while any HEAVY item is stowed, `run` is disabled, with no grams-based term and `V_CARRY` and `NOISE_PER_TICK` locked. The plate is therefore a priced second load, not a free second slot. AC-46 asserts the values derived below.)*
796	
797	**Derivation of the plate's price (constraint and arithmetic).** *Constraint:* the stowed plate must cost something a regression test can detect, without a mass term and without touching `V_CARRY` or `NOISE_PER_TICK`. The only free variable the ruling leaves is the empty-handed gait. With the plate stowed the empty gait drops from `V_RUN` 3 to `V_WALK` 2 px/tick, so the added time per tile is 48/2 - 48/3 = 24 - 16 = 8 ticks, a factor of 1.5. *Noise:* walking is quieter than running (1 against 4 per tick, so 24 against 64 per tile), so the plate does not add noise; it lengthens the exposure on the clock (the cost the player feels is time and, through Attention's time-based terms, the exposure that time carries), and Attention's X3 carry intake (keyed on HEAVY) is the route by which the burden becomes a legible stimulus, not this GDD. *While a module is carried* the gait is already `V_CARRY` 1, so the plate adds nothing: the price falls only on the empty-handed legs, which is the leg on which the free slot was free.
798	
799	**Example (plate stowed, 30 tiles, empty hands):** `ticks_empty_hs` = 30 x 48 / 2 = 720 ticks (12 s) and `noise_empty_hs` = 720 x 1 = 720; the same 30 tiles without the plate: `ticks_empty` = 480 ticks (8 s) and `noise_empty` = 1920. The plate costs +240 ticks (+50 percent) on a 30-tile empty leg and 1200 fewer noise units. With a carried `mod_reactor_cell` and the plate stowed: 1440 ticks and 1440 noise, identical to the carry without the plate. Passes the constraint: a regression that re-enables run changes 720 to 480. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Exact values with the run ramp:** the Controller's `RUN_RAMP_TICKS` 6 starts every run at `V_WALK` for 6 ticks (12 px), so the unplated 30-tile run is 6 + (1440 - 12) / 3 = **482 ticks** and 6 x 1 + 476 x 4 = **1910 noise units**; the figures 480 and 1920 above are the idealised no-ramp values, and the plate's exact cost on that leg is 720 - 482 = +238 ticks.
800	
801	**Pursuit exposure: what the plate actually costs** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Walking is always available, so the noise column understates the plate. The price is the **escape gait**: with a plate stowed the holder cannot reach `V_RUN`, so a pursuer whose speed `v_p` (px/tick, Horror Entities' number, not valued here) satisfies `V_WALK` <= `v_p` < `V_RUN` can be outrun by an unplated holder and cannot be outrun by a plated one; over a leg of `D` tiles a plated holder is exposed for `8 x D` extra ticks (48/2 - 48/3 per tile, ramp aside) and a pursuer covers `v_p x 8 x D` px more ground in that time. Over the 30-tile reference leg that is 240 extra ticks of exposure. The plate is therefore **slow to flee**, not loud: the MDA claim is reworded accordingly. **Attention C33 answered (this GDD's half)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*: Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling R5 (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): a stowed HEAVY item adds **no** `BURDEN` push. The burden is keyed on `carry_ref` (X3) and on salvage carry only (delegated ruling R5), a stowed plate is not a `carry_ref` carry, and charging it twice (burden for the gait it already lost) would double-price one cost; Attention keeps C33 closed on that reading and its refresh is owed no further change by the Item DB. **Single implementation:** the HEAVY-stowed test is Suit's `stowed_heavy(player_id)` (SE-41, which excludes units RESERVED by a FULL job and is derived on read), not a per-def check: the rule reads "any **unreserved** STOWED instance of `weight_class` HEAVY". A reserved plate (a FULL job holds it) therefore produces no run toggle, and no visible switch occurs when the reservation begins or is released early *(CD agreed with the gameplay-programmer: the earlier alternative rules would duplicate Suit)*. The Item DB's contribution is the class (`weight_class` HEAVY, F-1), Suit's is the sum and the reservation. **Reconciliation** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: D18's user wording is "any HEAVY item is stowed", Suit's `stowed_heavy` is sum-based (its stowed weight class is HEAVY), and IDB-13 was per-def. Under G1 the publisher's reading is canonical, so Suit's `stowed_heavy` is the implementation. In the MVP the readings coincide: the plate is the only HEAVY def, and the largest ordinary stack without it is 15,200 g, below `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` (AC-46 (iv)). The divergence case (a post-MVP stowed sum at or above `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` with no plate) is folded into Open Question 35 (Suit's class margin and hysteresis).
802	**Example:** a 30-tile trip carrying `mod_reactor_cell` (90000 g): `ticks_carry` = 30 x 48 / 1 = 1440 ticks (24 s) and `noise_carry` 1440; the same trip carrying `curio_data_core` (6000 g) is identical. The empty run out is 1440 / 3 = 480 ticks (8 s) and 1920 noise units; the round trip is 1920 ticks (32 s) and 3360 noise. Walking the same 30 tiles takes 720 ticks, so carrying costs twice the time and, per tile, twice the noise (48 vs 24).
803	
804	### F-14 Scrubber margin ladder (why a part is worth a sortie)
805	
806	The scrubber_margin formula is defined as:
807	
808	`margin(hp, N) = out_scr(hp) - N * R_BREATH` where `out_scr(hp)` is the Graph's D.5 evaluated at `sat` 1000 with `eff` from D.4 (cited, not restated) ; `scrubbers_to_hold(N, hp) = ceil(N * R_BREATH / out_scr(hp))` (the least count with margin >= 0) ; `scrubbers_with_margin(N, hp) = floor(N * R_BREATH / out_scr(hp)) + 1` (the least count with margin > 0, **strict-margin semantics, the design's standard**, because a margin of exactly zero "loses the room" at any wear: the Graph's own tuning note [LSG:927]) ; both return the sentinel `SCRUBBERS_UNDEFINED` = -1 when `out_scr(hp)` is 0, i.e. at or below `HP_FAIL` (no finite count exists) ; `T_hold = PATCH_DECAY_S` (240 s) is the maintenance interval of a life-critical scrubber at the patch ceiling: past it the patch decays and the margin goes negative, and duty wear (LSG:226) can shorten it ; `chore_per_hour_max = floor(3600 / T_hold)` re-patches, an **upper bound** (the earlier name `chore_per_hour` is retired), because it ignores the O2 tank buffer and the re-patch delay: the real interval is `T_hold` plus the time the tank takes to absorb the post-hold deficit, plus the player's reaction delay *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* ; `tank_steps(N, S, hp) = floor(stock / (N * R_BREATH - S * out_scr(hp)))` when the deficit `N * R_BREATH - S * out_scr(hp)` is positive, else `TANK_NEVER` (-1), with `stock` the O2 tank's stock (3,000,000 mGU at the shipped value) and 10 steps to the second (`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6 at `TICK_RATE` 60), which is the tank-drawdown model that replaces the 15-per-hour figure as the planning number *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: `scrubbers_needed` was off by one at exact divisibility — N = 4 at `hp` 10000 needs 3 scrubbers to reach margin 0 but 4 for a positive margin — and its UNDEFINED sentinel was not defined; the earlier `T_decay_cycle` 540 s as the maintenance interval was the time to FAILED, not the time to a negative margin, and understated the chore load by about 2.25x)*
809	
810	**Variables:**
811	
812	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
813	|---|---|---|---|---|
814	| `hp` | int bp | 0..`HP_FULL` | scrubber condition (the Graph) | Scrubber `hp` |
815	| `N` | int | 1..4 | the concept's 1-4 players | Crew breathing in the pool |
816	| `R_SCR` | int mGU/step | 400 (100-1000) | Graph data held in `mod_scrubber.rated_out` [LSG:927] | Scrubber nominal output |
817	| `R_BREATH` | int mGU/step | 300 (100-600) | Graph placeholder, owned by Suit & Equipment [LSG:929] | Draw per crew; read, never re-valued |
818	| `out_scr(hp)` | int mGU/step | 0..`R_SCR` | D.5 with D.4 (`HP_OK` 7000, `HP_FAIL` 3000) | Net output |
819	
820	**Output Range:** `margin` from -N x 300 up to +100 at N = 1 (a fully repaired scrubber). It is an analysis formula, not a runtime rule; if Suit moves `R_BREATH` the ladder moves with it and is not duplicated here.
821	**Example:** (N = 1, `sat` 1000) `hp` 10000 -> `eff` 1000 -> `out` 400 -> margin +100; `hp` 6000 (`PATCH_CAP_BP` [REG:6021-6037]) -> `eff` 750 -> `out` 300 -> margin **0**; `hp` 5000 -> 200 -> -100; `hp` 4000 -> 100 -> -200; `hp` 3000 -> 0 -> -300. So a patched scrubber supports exactly one crew with zero margin, and the part (which restores `hp_cap` to `HP_FULL` and ends the decay clock) buys +100 and the end of the chore. For two crew with one scrubber at `hp` 10000 the deficit is 600 - 400 = 200 mGU/step and the home-ship's 3,000,000 mGU O2 tank lasts 3,000,000 / 200 = 15,000 steps = 25 min; for four crew the deficit is 800 and the tank lasts 3750 steps = 6.25 min. **Those two figures need a `HP_FULL` scrubber, which the MVP cannot reach (no `part_machine_kit` is placed, F-11 scope note).** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **At the reachable ceiling, `PATCH_CAP_BP` 6000 (`out` 300):** N = 2 with one scrubber has a deficit of 600 - 300 = 300 mGU/step and the tank lasts 10,000 steps = 1,000 s = **16.7 min** (not 25); N = 4 has a deficit of 1200 - 300 = 900 and the tank lasts 3,333 steps = **5.6 min** (not 6.25); `scrubbers_to_hold(N, 6000)` = N and `scrubbers_with_margin(N, 6000)` = N + 1. The ladder rows that need 3 or 4 scrubbers (3,080 W and 3,680 W at 600 W each over the 1,880 W standing load) are beyond both the 2,500 W reactor and the 2,161 W trunk (Power budget under IDB-8): the MVP supports one crew member in steady state and treats N = 2 to 4 as timed on the tank. **Steady-state margin row and chore load** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: at N = 1 the margin falls by 10 mGU/step for every 100 bp below the patch ceiling (the rows above: 6000 -> 0, 5000 -> -100; the Graph's D.4 and D.5 are authoritative), so a patched scrubber at `hp` 6000 holds exactly its hold time `T_hold` 240 s and then runs negative: an **upper bound** of 15 re-patches per hour (`chore_per_hour_max`), not the 6 that a 540 s interval gave; the first 100 bp of decay is a deficit of only 10 mGU/step, which the full tank (3,000,000 mGU) absorbs for 300,000 steps (8.3 h), so a solo player's real re-patch interval is set by how fast the deficit grows and by the player's own margin of safety, not by `T_hold` alone *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; `scrubbers_to_hold(4, 10000)` = 3 (margin 0) and `scrubbers_with_margin(4, 10000)` = 4. This chore figure feeds Derelict Authoring's X-DA-9 and is a cross-GDD note. That is why derelict A's FAILED scrubber is the second scrubber a duo needs (a design reason and, since DA-47 / user ruling D72 gave `scr_a` a home slot, also an MVP route: the carry has a destination; the reference carry for the haul numbers stays `htr_a`, Boarding & Salvage C-BS-3) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Lever (reported to the Graph owner, not changed here): at `PATCH_CAP_BP` 5500 the patched `eff` is 625, `out` 250, margin -50 at N = 1, which makes the part mandatory even for a solo player.
822	
823	### F-15 Salvage-reinstall break-even (the launder regression tripwire)
824	
825	> **WITHDRAWN as a blocking item — retained as a historical note** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. F-15, AC-94 and `T_CYCLE_MIN` are no longer blocking and no longer gate anything. The review found the formula compared the cost of one salvage cycle against the whole patch chore over a horizon, which are not comparable; that its `T_decay_cycle` of 540 s understated the chore load (the life-critical interval is `T_hold` 240 s, see F-14); and that its tripwire is redundant now that IDB-18 closes the launder by rule and the split persistence tests AC-32a to AC-32f are the real control. The heading stays so the formula register (IDB-32) keeps its ids; the body below is kept for the record and is not a requirement.
826	
827	The patch_launder formula is defined as:
828	
829	`launder_pays_off <=> T_cycle < floor(H / T_decay_cycle) * (c_patch + w_patch)`
830	
831	**Variables:**
832	
833	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
834	|---|---|---|---|---|
835	| `T_cycle` | s | Interaction's and Assembly's | cut + carry + `cap_port` on the stubs + install | Time cost of one salvage-then-reinstall of a patched module |
836	| `H` | s | 1800-7200, design horizon | design | How long the module must stay serviceable |
837	| `T_decay_cycle` | s | 540 for a machine (to FAILED), 440 for a leak subject | Graph [LSG:769]: 240 s hold (`PATCH_DECAY_S`) plus 30 or 20 wear periods of 10 s at `PATCH_DECAY_BP_PER_100` 100 | Interval between mandatory re-patches |
838	| `c_patch`, `w_patch` | s | illustrative 8 and 15 | Interaction's channel time and walk (Interaction designed: `interaction-system.md`) | Cost of one re-patch |
839	
840	**Output Range:** boolean. Under the adopted rule (IDB-18: a reinstall carries `hp_cap` and `patched_at_step`) the launder does not exist, so this check is **no longer the control**; it is a regression tripwire and the Graph owner's fallback arithmetic. It answers one question: if a build or a ruling ever lets a reinstall reset the cap or the clock (`hp_cap` `HP_FULL`, no `patched_at_step`), would cycling pay? The primary control is the persistence rule and its test (AC-32: cap and clock must come back unchanged); this check is the second line. In no case does a cycle launder the damage (`hp` is unchanged) or duty wear.
841	**Example:** (all times illustrative until Interaction is written) *had the rule been the other way*: for a patched scrubber over `H` 3600 s, `T_decay_cycle` 540 gives floor(3600 / 540) = 6 re-patches x (8 + 15) = 138 s of chore, and a salvage-reinstall in one room at a 35 s illustrative `T_cycle` would be cheaper, so the launder would pay off at the placeholders, at the price of the cut's stub hiss (F-12: the scrubber's one O2 stub, port 101 per IDB-7, leaks 200 mGU/step until capped), the island re-solving without the scrubber and an Attention spike. That is exactly why the rule carries the cap and the clock: a free, repeatable action must not substitute for the finite part. If the Graph owner ever rules that a reinstall resets cap and clock, `T_CYCLE_MIN` 100 s becomes the only control and the placeholders already fail it (35 s against 100 s), so that ruling is not acceptable without a stronger sink and goes to creative-director review.
842	
843	
844	## Edge Cases
845	
846	Edge cases are grouped by theme. Diagnostics lines name only the **closed** failure list of IDB-30 (`ITEM_BOOT_TYPE_ID`, `ITEM_BOOT_FIELD`, `ITEM_BOOT_PORT`, `ITEM_BOOT_REPAIR`, `ITEM_BOOT_MIRROR`, `ITEM_BOOT_ALIAS`), the Graph's codes (`GRAPH_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF`, `PORT_INCOMPAT`, `NOT_REPAIRABLE`) or a named CI lint; the Item DB raises no runtime error and rejects no command, so a runtime refusal in a case below is always the owning neighbour's. Specialist proposals that invented other codes (a range code, a non-integer code, a forbidden-field code, a weight-margin code, an over-stack code) are mapped onto these.

847	
848	**Catalogue boot and ids**
849	
850	- **If two defs share a `def_id`, or two share a `type_id`**: boot is refused with `ITEM_BOOT_TYPE_ID(class, id)` naming the second occurrence. A catalogue with an ambiguous key cannot be loaded at all, because every save, hash and `SalvageRecord` is keyed by `def_id`.
851	- **If a `type_id` lies outside its prefix's class range (a `part_` def numbered 1xxx), or a `def_id` prefix disagrees with the declared class**: boot is refused with `ITEM_BOOT_TYPE_ID(class, id)` (F-8). The class ranges are what let the in-memory table be split by class without a lookup.
852	- **If a shipped def is renumbered (the ledger says `mod_scrubber` is 1001 and the data says 1020), or reuses a retired id**: boot is refused with `ITEM_BOOT_TYPE_ID`. A `type_id` never reaches a save, so a renumber could not break one, but the ledger keeps the in-memory ids stable for the vertical slice's replication summaries and makes reuse impossible.
853	- **If `hp_start` is 0 or above `HP_FULL`**: boot is refused with `ITEM_BOOT_FIELD(def_id, hp_start)` [IDB-9]. A node installed at `hp` 0 is a DESTROYED node leaking at its maximum [LSG:772].
854	- **If a JSON number arrives as `40000.5`, `1e9` or any non-integral value in an integer field**: boot is refused with `ITEM_BOOT_FIELD(def_id, field)`; an integral float such as `40000.0` is accepted and converted once at boot (`JSON.parse_string` returns numbers as floats, a MEDIUM-confidence engine claim, spike-bound). Zero floats may survive into the table (LS-1 (b)).
855	- **If a def carries a forbidden key (`price`, `damage`, `recipe`, `appears_as`, `hallucination_*` and the rest of IDB-5's list)**: boot is refused with `ITEM_BOOT_FIELD(def_id, field)`. The list is the machine form of the anti-pillars, so a later "just one price field" edit fails the build rather than a review.
856	- **If a def declares a `port_type_id` that is not in the Graph's LS-4 table, or one illegal for its node kind**: boot is refused with `ITEM_BOOT_PORT(def_id, local_index)`; the Graph's own boot would refuse the same table with `GRAPH_BOOT_TYPE_ID(table, id)`. The Item DB reports the def; the Graph reports the table.
857	- **If the LS-3 or LS-4 mirror in the catalogue differs from the Graph's boot table**: boot is refused with `ITEM_BOOT_MIRROR(table)`. The mirror is read-only; the Graph is the owner.
858	- **If an alias chain exceeds `ALIAS_DEPTH_MAX` 8, forms a cycle, points at itself, or names a live `def_id`**: boot is refused with `ITEM_BOOT_ALIAS(def_id)`. An alias never creates a def, and a retired string reused for a different def would let an old save silently load the wrong thing.
859	- **If a def with `mass_g` at or above `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` is authored with `stack_max` above 1, or a CARRIED/HAND def with `stack_max` above 1**: boot is refused with `ITEM_BOOT_FIELD(def_id, stack_max)`. A heavy stack would let a player carry an unbounded mass outside the single `carry_ref`.
860	- **If `repair_part_for` has no answer for one of the five `subject_kind` values, or a module names a `repair_part_id` that is not a part def, or `parts_per_full` is below 1**: boot is refused with `ITEM_BOOT_REPAIR(def_id)`. A FULL repair must never cost zero parts, and M7 may be handed any subject kind.
861	
862	**Zero, maximum and out-of-range values**
863	
864	- **If a catalogue edit lowers `stack_max` below a count already held in a save**: the restore **keeps the full held count and deletes nothing**; the holder refuses further pickups of that def until the count is at or below the new maximum. This is the one invariant of IDB-15 that is not asserted at restore (it stays a lint at serialise). (orchestrator ruling: the economy proposal's keep-and-refuse-pickup over the systems proposal's clamp, because a silent clamp destroys items without the player doing anything, against Pillar 5's "loss is not total".)
865	- **If a module `ItemInstance` is serialised with `condition_bp` 0, or above `cap_bp`, or a `cap_bp` of 0, or a non-zero `patched_at_step` on a `cap_bp` of `HP_FULL`, or a `patched_at_step` of 0 on a `cap_bp` below `HP_FULL`, or a `patched_at_step` above the holder's current `step_no`**: the holder's restore refuses it with the holder's own named failure (the Item DB provides the check, not the code). A `cap_bp` of 9999 is **valid** (a patched module whose recorded cap is any value below `HP_FULL`; there is no tie to the current `PATCH_CAP_BP`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier "neither `HP_FULL` nor at most `PATCH_CAP_BP`" form refused every saved patched module after a `PATCH_CAP_BP` retune)*. A module at `hp` 0, DESTROYED or FAILED-at-`hp`-0 (legal while the Graph's warning gate is closed), yields a part, never a module (F-5; cutting a FAILED `hp`-0 node scraps it) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, BLOCKING)*, so a zero-condition module instance can only be corruption; a non-canonical zero would give one state two byte forms and desync `state_hash`.
866	- **If `mass_g` or a `WEIGHT_*` threshold is edited between builds, and a def now falls in a different `weight_class`**: nothing migrates and nothing bumps `catalogue_version`. Mass and class are never persisted on an instance (IDB-15), so the next read re-derives them; a boundary case is caught earlier by the `WEIGHT_CLASS_MARGIN_PM` lint (F-1).
867	- **If an instance's `count` would exceed `stack_max` on a merge**: the merge is refused by the holder (Suit) and the surplus stays where it was; the Item DB supplies the cap and nothing else. A pickup refused for a full stack leaves the item in the world, so scarcity never silently deletes salvage.
868	- **If a FULL repair targets a subject already at `hp_cap` = `HP_FULL` with `hp` = `hp_cap`**: it consumes nothing and Interaction resolves `PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR)` [IDB-20 (1); IA-18 statement 7]. A part must change something to be spent.
869	
870	**Simultaneous rules**
871	
872	- **If two players cut the same node on the same tick**: the first applied M6 yields the module; the second M6 sees SALVAGED and is rejected under validate-then-apply [KRN:CR-9], so `salvage_yield` runs once on the applied record and the module cannot be duplicated. The yield is computed from the M6 return value, never from a pre-read of the node (F-5).
873	- **If two players start a FULL repair on one subject, each with one part, on the same step**: commands dispatch sequentially, so the first begin is Applied (its part RESERVED at the begin tick, then PAID at its first productive step) and the second seat's begin is `BUSY` at `validate` and makes no reservation, so the second player's visible stock never falls (Interaction IA-34; registry `full_job_charge`). Each player's part is spent only if that player's first step is applied (IDB-20 (7)).
874	- **If a FULL repair channel is interrupted (stagger, pod hop) after its first productive step**: the part stays spent and the `hp` already applied stays; the Item DB gives no refund. Interaction's `FULL_JOB_GRACE_S` (60 s, IA-18 statement 6) waives the charge when the same seat re-issues on the same subject inside the window; after it, or for another seat, the second attempt costs `parts_per_full` again.
875	- **If a PATCH step is issued inside a paid FULL job**: it would re-cap `hp_cap` to `PATCH_CAP_BP` and waste the part [LSG:186]; a FULL job must issue only `kind = FULL` steps (IDB-20 (2)), and the acceptance test asserts it.
876	- **If a player tries `begin_patch` or `begin_cut` while holding `carry_ref`**: Interaction rejects it `BUSY` under PC-8 [PCI:131, 168]; the player must `drop` first. This is why `part_hull_plate` is STOWED with `stack_max` 1: a stowed part never sets `carry_ref`, so the part itself can never be what blocks the full repair that consumes it.
877	
878	**Degenerate strategies**
879	
880	- **If a player salvages a patched module and reinstalls it to shed the patch ceiling and decay clock**: it sheds neither. The module reinstalls with its record's `hp`, `hp_cap` at `PATCH_CAP_BP` and the original `patched_at_step`, so the cap stays and the clock keeps its origin (IDB-18, settled by the Graph's LS-18 M5/M6 amendment) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Time in transit counts toward the hold: a module carried or shelved longer than `PATCH_DECAY_S` 240 s reinstalls already past its hold and starts decaying at the next wear period. The only way to lift the cap is a FULL repair and its part. The cut still costs the hissing stubs, the island re-solving, a flat-speed carry and an Attention spike, so there is no reason to cycle; the split persistence tests AC-32a to AC-32f guard the regression (the `T_CYCLE_MIN` tripwire is withdrawn, F-15).
881	- **If a player deliberately destroys a spare module (overload, dropped into a breach) to harvest its part**: a DESTROYED node salvages into exactly `scrap_count` (1) of its `repair_part_id` and no module, so one module becomes one part at most; the conversion costs a module, which is itself finite salvage. Part conservation (IDB-29 (2)) holds: parts in existence never exceed authored loose parts plus DESTROYED module nodes. The conversion is not value-aware: a destroyed lamp yields the same scarce `part_cable_splice` as a destroyed breaker, so destruction is a (costly) parts source that F-11 prints as `supply_max` (whether to make scrap tier-aware, or to rule that fixtures cannot be destroyed on purpose, is Open Question 39) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
882	- **If a player salvages the running SCRUBBER or the live BATTERY**: it is allowed with no special case [LSG:773]; the island re-solves, the stubs hiss, the item is delivered whole. A reinstalled store starts empty (IDB-18), so a battery carried home is dark until recharged. The world shows the cost.
883	- **If a player hoards glowsticks or parts**: the holder caps each stack at `GLOWSTICK_STACK_MAX` 4 and the part `stack_max`; a stack that is full refuses the pickup. Light and permanent fixes stay a decision, not a stockpile, and the stowed mass is a body cue only.
884	- **If a player tries to run with a carried module**: not an Item DB rule; the Controller forbids it (PC-8) and mass never changes the 1 px/tick carry speed or the carry noise (F-13). A request for mass-scaled speed is a registry conflict, not a tuning change.
885	- **If a player tries to run while the hull plate is stowed** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: `run` is refused for as long as any unreserved HEAVY STOWED instance is held (IDB-13, D18; Suit's `stowed_heavy`, SE-41, excludes units a FULL job has RESERVED) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; the holder walks at `V_WALK`. The gait returns on the tick the plate leaves the stowed stock (the shed of States row 14, or the reservation at the begin tick of the FULL job that consumes it, F-4). A DOWNED seat keeps its stowed stock (States row 15) and, on a revive, still cannot run. Picking a plate up from the floor re-disables run on the pickup tick. The rule reads the def class, so it is unaffected by the glowsticks and parts in the same pack.
886	
887	**Save, restore and catalogue edits**
888	
889	- **If a save names a `def_id` that was removed with no `replaced_by`**: the Graph's restore fails with `GRAPH_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF` [LSG:832] for a node, or the holder's own named failure for an instance, with live state untouched. Never a silent drop (IDB-27). Diagnostics: the failing `def_id` and the save's `catalogue_version`.
890	- **If a removed def has `replaced_by`, or a renamed def has `renamed_from`**: restore maps the instance or node to the successor and keeps `condition_bp` / `hp`. Aliases are honoured only at restore (IDB-4, IDB-27).
891	- **If a save was written under a higher `catalogue_version` than the running catalogue**: Save/Load's pre-check does not refuse and the holder's restore decides (Save/Load SL-14 [SL:219]: "a header `catalogue_version` above or below the running catalogue's is never a pre-check refusal; the load proceeds and each holder's `restore()` decides; an unknown `def_id` stays the owning block's named failure (`GRAPH_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF`); a `renamed_from` alias honoured only at restore is the Item DB's to offer"; AC-SL-96e [SL:1220]: `catalogue_version` 9 in the header against 7 in the running catalogue); the Item DB offers the integer and states that pre-release saves are disposable [LSG:832].
892	- **If the catalogue edits `req_w` (or another snapshotted-at-install field) of `mod_scrubber` and a save holds an installed scrubber**: the saved node keeps its old value until it is salvaged and reinstalled (IDB-6); no bump. **If it edits `waste_permille`, `R_SCR`, `BATT_CELL` or `cap_ml`** and the Graph reads those live, the change applies to existing saves at the next restore, a possible mid-game rebalance. The Graph ruled "read live through `def_id`" (its Item DB Interactions row; Open Question 8 closed). The one live-read edit with a consequence is a lowered `stock_cap`: stock above the new cap moves to `discarded_*` and is logged at restore (IDB-6, Open Question 31) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
893	- **If a catalogue retune lowers `stock_cap` below the stock a saved node holds** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: on restore the excess above the live cap moves to the section's `discarded_*` counter (conserved) and is logged; it is never a restore refusal and never silent (IDB-6 "Restore against a retuned catalogue"; Open Question 31; AC-105, BLOCKED-ON the Graph).
894	- **If `PATCH_CAP_BP` is retuned after a save holds a patched module** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the saved `cap_bp` (for example 6000 against a new 5500) restores and reinstalls unchanged; the invariant is `cap_bp < HP_FULL`, with no tie to the constant; the next PATCH takes `min(hp_cap, PATCH_CAP_BP)`, and a PATCH on `hp` at or above the new cap is refused `ABOVE_PATCH_CAP` with `hp` never clamped down (AC-106).
895	- **If the crew dies while carrying a module**: MVP death is restart from the last autosave (user decision; Save/Load owns it, SL-7), so the restore replays every holder block and no item-loss rule exists in the Item DB. The module is wherever the autosave had it.
896	- **If a section holding loose items or installed modules is discarded**: `discard_section` (M4 [LSG:183]) discards them with the section and destroys their mass into `discarded_*` [LSG:799]; the Item DB defines no refund. It is the loss sink of "ship, not knowledge".

898	**Salvage, ports and hardpoints (checkpoint-born)**

915	- **If a phantom crate is dressed as a data core (class d, vertical slice) and picked up**: the carry body cue reports the junk def's true `mass_g` (a different class by F-10); the player can disprove the lie by weight before the trip home. 917	- **If a player asks what a held item "really is" under hallucination**: the def's identity is never hidden behind an identify step (Player Fantasy); the only uncertainty is Pillar 4 perception, which has a cheaper falsifier (weight) than the trip home.

920	
921	- **If a downed player was carrying a module**: the Controller drops it as a loose item at that position (PCI PC-8); the instance persists as LOOSE_WORLD and a teammate may pick it up. 1060	## Visual/Audio Requirements
1061	
1062	*Scope note.* The Item DB is data: it renders nothing and plays nothing. This section states what the player must be able to **see and hear because of the catalogue**, which GDD draws or sounds it, and which art bible sections bind it. No art-director proposal file and no audio proposal exists for this stage (the stage brief lists none), so the art-direction questions are routed to Open Questions rather than invented here. Citations use the keys of the Overview; "ART n.n" is an art bible section.
1063	
1064	**What the player sees, and the rule behind it.** (1) *Condition is drawn, never labelled.* A salvaged module shows the wear it came with as scuffs worn to bare metal at rounded corners (Foundry, ART 6.1) and a bolted patch plate that straddles panel lines "on-grid and off-rhythm" after a PATCH (ART 6.1, [ART:617]); permitted materials are cold metals only (ART 6.2, [ART:635]). No bar, number or colour code states condition (IDB-21, G3). (2) *A dead module is a stopped machine.* A FAILED scrubber is dark, its rotor still and no medium moving (ART design principle 2); the catalogue never "refreshes" it (IDB-9, IDB-24), so the sprite family is the same def at a lower `hp`, not a `_dead` variant. (3) *Parts read like the loop they mend*: a duct coupling reads O2, a cable splice reads power, a pipe fitting reads coolant by silhouette and loop hue, hue redundant with shape ([CON:343-345]); the hue is the art-director's token, the shape is the `sprite_family` key. (4) *Tools are silhouettes.* A hand tool is a sprite drawn once per tool, never per dialect (ART 5.1, [ART:512]); its hand-rail glyph is that sprite reduced to the 16 px grid (ART 7.2, [ART:815]), so `glyph_id` names a derived asset, not a hand-made icon. (5) *The carry frame keeps the chest lamp clear*: a carried module rides above the helmet and never covers the chest point (ART 5.1, [ART:512]), and a heavy stowed part (the hull plate) is drawn on the back rig under the same rule; no bare skin, no body shown ([ART:508]). (6) *Sane-palette discipline*: no item, part, tool or glowstick uses flesh or violet, which are reserved for sanity leaks ([CON:333-334]); there is no rarity colour, because there is no rarity (IDB-5, IDB-29). (7) *Footprint*: every def draws in one of the five sprite cells (`M96`, `P48`, `P48x96`, `P96x48`, `T80`; ART 8.2) named by the grammar of ART 8.5.

1085	**Audio, stated plainly.** The catalogue adds **no sound design of its own**. The three sounds that matter are owned elsewhere: the cut hiss (Graph leak plus Adaptive Audio and Tells), the carry footfall (the Controller's carry noise, which is flat per tile and never scales with mass), and the running or silent state of an installed machine (the machine's own state). One rule binds every audio author who touches an item: **a sound must never encode value or hidden condition** — no rare-item chime, no "this one is broken" cue — because that would be a hidden stat leaking through the audio channel (P1) and a free sane-channel substitute for the P4(b) field check. The only item sound that is information is the one the world would make anyway.

1091	## Game Feel
1092	
1093	*Ownership note.* The catalogue has no input, no animation and no frame data, so the feel of its things is owned elsewhere: the **carry** by the Controller (`V_CARRY`, PC-8), the **body cue** for mass by Suit & Equipment, the **channelled repair, cut and throw** by the Interaction System, the **glowstick light** by Emitter State. What this GDD owns is the *data that makes those feels honest*: a true mass, a true class, a true condition and a finite part. Every target below is therefore a requirement on a neighbour, tagged with the neighbour, and nothing here is a number the Item DB can tune except where a knob is named. Ticks are 60 Hz; steps are 10 Hz.
1094	
1095	### Feel Reference
1096	
1097	The target is the moment in **Project Zomboid** when a player drags a heavy generator or a stack of planks across a yard: the cost is the **trip**, not a number — slower, louder, hands busy, every sound behind you suddenly relevant — and the thing keeps the damage it already had. Borrow that, and borrow **Pandorum's** hands-free chest lamp: the beam stays on the road while both arms hold the load. The anti-reference is the **encumbrance meter** (a weight bar that gently scales speed) and the **inventory grid**: weight here is never a readout and never a gradient, and nothing is "managed" in a menu. A second anti-reference is the **loot pop** (a glint, a chime, a rarity colour at pickup): picking a thing up is a quiet, physical act whose meaning arrives later, at the install.
1098	
1099	### Input Responsiveness
1100	
1101	The Item DB adds no input. The item actions below are the Controller's and Interaction's; the row states the feel requirement the catalogue's data imposes on them. Latencies are proposals for those GDDs to adopt or replace (Interaction designed: `interaction-system.md`).

1106	| `drop` a carried module | the next tick | 1 tick | `drop` is the one mode PC-8 accepts while carrying; it must never be `BUSY` |
1107	| Any other `interact` while carrying | rejected `BUSY` on the same tick | 1 tick | The refusal is immediate and legible (Controller's feedback), never silent |
1108	| `throw_glowstick` | the arc starts on the next tick; lands after `THROW_ARC_TICKS` 30 | 1 tick, then 30 | The stick counts life from the throw tick (F-7), so a quick re-throw does not waste light |
1109	| Use or start a FULL repair | the channel starts on the next tick if a part is held | 1 tick | The part is spent at the first **productive** step, not at button press (IDB-20) |
1110	| Hand-rail swap to a tool | the next tick | 1 tick | The glyph and the hand sprite change together |

1124	### Impact Moments
1125	
1126	There is no hit-stop, shake or rumble in this system: a survival-horror economy earns its beats from **consequence**, not punctuation. The moments of peak feedback are all world events the catalogue's data causes.

1136	
1137	### Weight and Responsiveness Profile
1138	
1139	- **Weight**: Heavy and deliberate for a module; unremarkable for a part, tool or glowstick. The weight is expressed as a **gait and a cost in sound and exposure**, never as a number, a bar or a pop-up. A 90 kg reactor cell and a 6 kg data core cost the same per tile (F-13); the body cue (Suit) is where their masses differ. The 30 kg hull plate on the hauler's back rig is the other visible weight: it is seen on the back frame and felt as the same closed-list body cue (IDB-21), never as a number.
1140	- **Player control**: High. Even while carrying, the player can steer, aim the chest lamp and `drop` on any tick; the only things they lose are the run and the other `interact` modes. The load commits the player to a path, not to an animation.
1141	- **Snap quality**: Analog for the burn of a glowstick (a smooth waning), binary for installs and part spending (it is done, or it is not).
1142	- **Acceleration model**: Simulation feel. The carry gait is a flat `V_CARRY` 1 px/tick taken the tick `carry_ref` is set (the Controller's ramp, `RUN_RAMP_TICKS`, applies to run only [PCI:296-319]); the catalogue adds no acceleration term of its own.
1143	- **Failure texture**: Fair and readable. A repair fails for a reason the world shows: the part is missing (the stowed stack has none), the subject is DESTROYED (no plate to patch), or the cap is reached (the module runs but remains DEGRADED). A lost module is never a surprise: a dropped or abandoned module is still on the floor with its condition unchanged.

Protocol for all of them: a scripted session, eight or more testers, scored against a written key, evidence file `production/qa/evidence/item-db/et-protocol-[date].md` retained.)*

1155	- [ ] At least 6 of 8 testers pick "heavy" or "committing" over "floaty", "free" or "speed penalty bar" for a carried module on a forced-choice pair; the haul is described as slow to flee and committing.
1156	- [ ] No playtester can read a mass, a condition number or a rarity from any surface (G3, G4), yet can tell a heavy thing from a light one by the body cue once Suit exists.
1157	- [ ] (Vertical slice, ET-5) At least 6 of 8 testers who carried a phantom crate home say "it felt too light" or "I should have checked".

1159	## UI Requirements
1160	
1161	**The Item DB has no UI of its own.** It is a static catalogue (IDB-1) with no screen, menu, inventory view, weight readout or condition bar, and it must never acquire one (guard rails G1-G3 and ruling R8: no pack capacity and no weight readout in the MVP; the concept itself is silent on an inventory screen, so this is a decision of this GDD, to be confirmed by the HUD GDD). It supplies exactly **two string keys** to surfaces other GDDs own: `glyph_id` (the tool's 16 px silhouette, ART 7.2) and `name_key` (a plain technician-register localisation key, IDB-5), plus the true `mass_g` and `weight_class` that Suit turns into a body cue rather than text. Every surface below is owned by the GDD in the last column, and each of those GDDs must repeat the clause it takes from this table in its own Interactions row (AC-63, AC-96).

Every edited paragraph and row carries "*(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*" or "*(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling Rn)*". *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
152:**EM-5 — Nobody writes emitters directly.** Records are created, changed and destroyed only through the published mutators below, each callable inside a kernel `WriteScope` (CR-9) by its declared caller, and by `emitter.place` itself for the two derived kinds. Lighting, Attention, Horror, the Perception Filter and every presentation subscriber never create, move, switch or delete an emitter (kernel C.3 row 7: "Lighting never writes emitters"). *Class A* mutators are infallible applies inside a caller's validated command; *Class B* mutators clamp and never reject, and an unknown id is a no-op returning 0/false (the Graph's precedent, LS-18). A creation mutator fills every derived field of the new record (origin = anchor, `output_pm` and `reach_px` by EM-11 / EM-14 / EM-15 / EM-16, `lit` from `output_pm`) so a record created in tick T is complete in the read view from P4 of T even when the creating hook runs after `emitter.place`; only the *subject table* trails (a new emitter enters exposure evaluation at the first `emitter.place` run at or after its creation, at most one tick later, inside PC-5's committed-versus-drawn tolerance).
220:**EM-14 — Node lanterns are derived and switchless.** A NODE_LANTERN stands for the glow of a running machine (every machine node whose def carries an `emits` with shape `LANTERN`; the kinds are Item DB data, IDB-31, not a list in this rule: in the MVP a reactor cell, a coolant pump and a scrubber). E1 creates one NODE_LANTERN per such node, and nothing in this rule restricts the kind; the shape key stays `LANTERN` and the hue is per loop (`LANTERN_POWER`, `LANTERN_COOLANT`, `LANTERN_O2`). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* It has no switch and makes no `set_load_request` call: `output_pm` is `⌊base_pm * term / 1000⌋` when the node is live and *running* (Formulas D.3 `node_lantern_output`), where `term` is the node's `run_pm` reading. A lantern gated on `served_pm` alone would glow from a switched-off machine (the same trap as EM-11), so the lantern reads a *running* quantity `run_pm` from the Graph read view — **delivered by the Graph** (LS-19 additions, 2026-10-27: `node(id).run_pm`, 0..1000 — 0 when the requested load is 0 (LOAD `req_w` 0, PUMP `throttle_pm` 0, REACTOR `out_w` 0), otherwise `served_pm` for a consumer and `⌊1000 × out_w / out_w_rated⌋` for a REACTOR; it is not the Graph's D.9 `duty_pm`, which reads 1000 for a machine switched off on a met tier and carries the same trap as EM-11). The Emitter **consumes `run_pm` as published and clamps it** to 0..1000 (D.3): it never recomputes it from `out_w`, so a REACTOR running above rated output cannot make a lantern outshine its `base_pm`, and a rated output of 0 is the Graph's guard, not an Emitter division. 204:**SE-12. Holder model.** *Rule.* Suit owns the three holder classes defined by the Item DB (IDB-16 "the Item DB defines what a thing is; the holder owns who has it and how many"): **HAND** (tool instances — unique per player, one of each `tool_*`, `stack_max` 1), **STOWED** (counted entries in the block, one stack per `def_id`, merged per IDB-15 when `def_id`, `condition_bp` and `charge` are equal), and **CARRIED** (the single carried instance — the Controller owns `carry_ref`, Suit owns the instance and the stored `carried_id`). All modules and the curio are CARRIED; tools are HAND; parts and glowsticks are STOWED. A refused merge leaves the surplus where it was ("the merge is refused by the holder (Suit) and the surplus stays where it was"). The persisted, hashed and replicated form of every instance Suit holds is the Item DB's positional array from `to_array()` = [def_id, count, condition_bp, cap_bp, patched_at_step, charge] (always six elements, every number an int, canonical zeros), decoded only by `from_array(a, graph_step_no)`; Suit never hand-builds an instance Dictionary *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: Item DB IDB-15, registry `item_instance_to_array`; Suit adopts the owner's published canonical form)*; masses and classes are looked up from the static catalogue and never saved. **Suit mints no ids**: the only id it stores is the carried one, passed in by `set_carried`; stowed stacks carry no ids. There is no pack capacity and no weight limit — the carrying cost is the mass cue (SE-28) and, for a carried module, the Controller's `V_CARRY` (no run). *Why.* One owner for "who holds what"; a pack grid or weight cap is an inventory screen by another name (Item DB OQ 6). *Rejected.* A pack grid or total-weight cap. *Criterion.* AC-SE-14: a merge-and-refuse table test over `part_hull_plate` (×1), `part_duct_coupling` (×4) and `cons_glowstick` (×4). *Pillar.* P5, anti-pillar no inventory.
206:**SE-13. The carried instance and the one mover.** *Rule.* `set_carried(player_id, instance_id, instance)` stores the instance; `release_carried(player_id)` removes it and returns `(instance_id, instance)`, where `instance` is the six-element `to_array()` array of SE-12, stored and returned with every element unchanged (the identity rule, so the Interaction launder fix holds end to end) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. **Suit never self-releases.** On `locomotion_cap` NONE the Controller clears `carry_ref` and **Interaction** converts it to a loose item next tick by calling `release_carried`. Stagger does not drop the module; downed does. `post_restore` checks `controller.state.carry_ref == suit.state.carried_id` (or both NONE) and fails `SUIT_RESTORE_CARRY_MISMATCH` otherwise. The loose-world owner and the instance-id counter are not Suit's: Interaction's designed IA-28 owns `loose[]` and the id counter in `interaction.state`; Suit stores only the id it is handed, and its text holds under any owner. *Why.* Exactly one mover prevents a module existing in two holders at once. *Rejected.* Suit allocating ids (two allocators collide). *Criterion.* AC-SE-15: a carry dropped on DOWNED round-trips to a loose item with identical instance fields; a restore with a mismatched `carry_ref` fails with the named reason. *Pillar.* P1 (the world holds each thing once).

art-bible.md
8:> **Last Verified**: 2026-10-27 (re-review read-through of the epoch, thread, formula and acceptance sections)
161:| `catalogue_version` | int | Item/module content epoch — the Item & Module Database's name (designed; IDB-26 `meta.json` key, IDB-27, its Save/Load row; history OQ-13). `catalogue_hash` (hex) is diagnostic only |
239:**SL-14 — Versioning and migration (D7).** Two levels. **Container** `format_version` (from 1, `FORMAT_VERSION`) is migrated by Save/Load; **block** `schema_version` is migrated by the *owner* inside `restore(data, stored_version)` as a chain v → v+1 → …, each step a registered pure function `(old dictionary) → new dictionary`. **Save/Load never rewrites a block's data itself** — owners are the only writers of their shape. Save/Load verifies, in the pre-check (T-5 step "schema chain"), that the chain is complete for every stored block (a gap is `SL_PRECHECK_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED`, never a mid-restore failure). A migrated payload is **not written back** to the old generation file; the next autosave writes the new shape, so a downgrade followed by an upgrade cannot half-migrate a file. A persisted WORLD block is **mandatory** for a file iff its registration's `added_in_format ≤ file.format_version`; the MVP mandatory set (SL-25) is the *expected result* of that rule, not a hand-kept list. An **additive bump** — a new block added after the first outside build — is `format_version + 1`, `min_reader_version` = the new version, container migration = identity, the new block filled by `default_state()`; defining it keeps the friction of adding a block constant. `added_in_format`, `RETIRED_BLOCKS` and the mandatory flag live in one data file cross-checked against the live registry at boot (→ ADR candidate). **Policy:** the machinery exists from format 1 and two goldens are kept *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a **stand-in golden** in `tests/fixtures/saves/v1-standin/`, regenerated freely while the registry is still moving (it exercises the machinery, not any shipped shape), and a **frozen golden** in `tests/fixtures/saves/v1/`, generated from the real registry at the first outside build and immutable from then on, with a schema-drift fingerprint check in CI (the committed shapes' `registry_epoch` digest may change only together with a `schema_version` or `format_version` bump) — the Graph's acceptance criterion names the convention; the **obligation** to migrate begins with the first build given to anyone outside the project (the three-person MVP playtest); earlier development saves are disposable and are refused with "made by an incompatible development build" *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the signal is the header `registry_epoch` — a file whose epoch differs from ours and fails a mandatory-set or schema step is INCOMPATIBLE-dev and never quarantined, so registering one more block does not turn every dev save into a quarantined CORRUPT file)*. That policy is Save/Load's own; the Graph's citation of a Layout open question ("pre-release saves are disposable") is answered from the Layout side *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass)*: a renamed `room_key` or `template_id` needs a migration step in the owner once the first build has been given outside the project; before that, saves are disposable (this rule; OQ-12 closed). After the policy begins, a rename of a `def_id` or a `room_id` needs a migration step in its owner. The header's `catalogue_version` (designed — Item & Module Database, IDB-26, IDB-27) lets the owner detect a content-epoch change. findings.section: IDB-31 / AC-26 / AC-97 vs Emitter State E1 (new consequence of the scrubber-lantern ruling)
findings.finding: IDB-31 and AC-26 say a node lantern is carried by every node whose def carries emits LANTERN. Emitter State E1 runs only at init_world (Web Map WM-24; install_module and cut call no Emitter mutator), and DA OQ-DA-55 leaves the slot-installed scr_a lantern undecided. So a scr_a installed in the vacant home scrubber slot (DA-47, an MVP beat and the ET-2 measurement) gets no lantern, while scr_main has one. findings.fix: Add to IDB-31 and AC-26 that the lantern contract covers init_world nodes only until OQ-DA-55 is decided, and cross-reference OQ-DA-55 (owner: Emitter writer). Scope AC-26's 'exactly the nodes' clause and AC-97 to authored nodes, and add a pending AC for the slot-installed case.

findings.section: IDB-31 / AC-26 / AC-97 vs Emitter State E1 (new consequence of the scrubber-lantern ruling)
findings.finding: IDB-31 and AC-26 say a node lantern is carried by every node whose def carries emits LANTERN. Emitter State E1 runs only at init_world (Web Map WM-24; install_module and cut call no Emitter mutator), and DA OQ-DA-55 leaves the slot-installed scr_a lantern undecided. So a scr_a installed in the vacant home scrubber slot (DA-47, an MVP beat and the ET-2 measurement) gets no lantern, while scr_main has one. A patched, DEGRADED scr_a at home would run with no glow: the lie by omission the ruling was meant to prevent. The Item DB text does not say this.
findings.fix: Add to IDB-31 and AC-26 that the lantern contract covers init_world nodes only until OQ-DA-55 is decided, and cross-reference OQ-DA-55 (owner: Emitter writer). Scope AC-26's 'exactly the nodes' clause and AC-97 to authored nodes, and add a pending AC for the slot-installed case.
